1	"""Benchmark recipe schema, result types, and the benchmark registry.
2	
3	A benchmark recipe is a declarative YAML file under ``recipes/benchmarks/``.  It
4	maps 1:1 onto NeMo Evaluator's ``@benchmark`` decorator fields (``dataset`` URI,
5	``prompt`` template, ``target_field``, a ``scorer`` chosen from the scorer
6	library) so upstream benchmark definitions port directly into YAML, with a ``.py``
7	scorer escape hatch for the long tail that needs code.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
13	from pathlib import Path
14	from typing import Any, Literal
15	
16	import yaml
17	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
18	
19	from ..logging_util import RecipeError
20	
21	_RECIPE_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "recipes" / "benchmarks"
22	
23	
24	class CodeExecSpec(BaseModel):
25	    """Config for the ``code_exec`` scorer (LiveCodeBench / HumanEval / MBPP family).
26	
27	    The model's completion is extracted, assembled with the sample's test code into
28	    one program, executed in a sandbox, and scored 1.0 iff it exits cleanly. Field
29	    names map onto the dataset columns (HumanEval defaults shown).
30	    """
31	
32	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
33	
34	    language: str = "python"
35	    interpreter: str = "python3"
36	    timeout_s: float = 30.0
37	    extract: bool = True  # pull the fenced ```python block out of the completion
38	    include_prompt: bool = False  # prepend the prompt/signature to the completion
39	    prompt_field: str = "prompt"
40	    test_field: str = "test"
41	    entry_point_field: str = "entry_point"
42	    check_template: str = "\ncheck({entry_point})\n"
43	    preamble: str | None = None  # code prepended to every program (imports, helpers)
44	
45	
46	class JudgeSpec(BaseModel):
47	    """Config for the ``llm_judge`` scorer (LLM-as-judge / rubric grading).
48	
49	    The judge is any OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint. ``template`` is the user
50	    message rendered per sample with ``{question}``/``{prediction}``/``{target}``/
51	    ``{scale}`` fields; the judge is asked to emit ``SCORE: <0..scale>`` which we
52	    normalise to ``[0, 1]``. Set ``threshold`` to binarise (raw score >= threshold
53	    -> 1.0 else 0.0) for pass/fail style rubrics.
54	    """
55	
56	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
57	
58	    model: str = "gpt-4o-mini"
59	    base_url: str | None = None  # defaults to OPENAI_BASE_URL env, else OpenAI
60	    api_key_env: str = "OPENAI_API_KEY"
61	    system: str | None = None
62	    template: str | None = None
63	    scale: float = 10.0
64	    threshold: float | None = None
65	    temperature: float = 0.0
66	    max_tokens: int = 512
67	
68	
69	class ScoringSpec(BaseModel):
70	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
71	
72	    # A built-in/registered scorer name, OR a "path.py:func" escape hatch.
73	    scorer: str | None = None
74	    # lm_eval harness reads the metric straight from its own results json.
75	    metric: str | None = None
76	    prefer: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
77	    # Config for scorer == "llm_judge" (ignored otherwise).
78	    judge: JudgeSpec | None = None
79	    # Config for scorer == "code_exec" (ignored otherwise).
80	    code_exec: CodeExecSpec | None = None
81	
82	
83	class BenchmarkRecipe(BaseModel):
84	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
85	
86	    name: str
87	    harness: str = "lm_eval"  # native | lm_eval | evalscope(plugin)
88	    type: Literal["generative", "loglikelihood", "multichoice", "qa"] = "loglikelihood"
89	
90	    # lm_eval routing: the registered lm_eval task name (defaults to `name`).
91	    lm_eval_task: str | None = None
92	    apply_chat_template: bool = False
93	    fewshot_as_multiturn: bool = False
94	    num_fewshot: int | None = None
95	    gen_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
96	    batch_size: str | None = None  # per-task batch size override (else harness default)
97	
98	    # native harness routing.
99	    dataset: str | None = None  # e.g. hf://openai/gsm8k?split=test
100	    prompt: str | None = None  # e.g. "{question}"
101	    target_field: str | None = None
102	
103	    # diffusion harness routing: prompt column in `dataset` (HF uri or local file).
104	    prompt_field: str = "Prompts"
105	
106	    scoring: ScoringSpec = Field(default_factory=ScoringSpec)
107	    description: str = ""
108	
109	    def task_name(self) -> str:
110	        return self.lm_eval_task or self.name
111	
112	
113	@dataclass
114	class BenchmarkResult:
115	    name: str
116	    score: float
117	    metric: str
118	    num_samples: int = 0
119	    per_sample: list[float] | None = None  # per-sample correctness (0/1) for paired stats
120	    raw: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
121	    command: str = ""  # the exact harness command that produced this result
122	    stats: Any = None  # optional TokenStats (agentic benchmarks); efficiency provenance
123	    turns: int = 0     # total agent turns spent (agentic benchmarks)
124	
125	    @classmethod
126	    def from_agent_result(cls, agent_result: Any, *, name: str,
127	                          metric: str = "resolved_rate") -> BenchmarkResult:
128	        """Bridge an ``AgentEvalResult`` into a benchmark row.
129	
130	        Carries the agentic score plus its efficiency provenance (token totals +
131	        turns), so an agentic benchmark folded into an :class:`EvalResult` lands
132	        in the reproducibility manifest's ``efficiency`` block automatically.
133	        """
134	        return cls(
135	            name=name,
136	            score=agent_result.mean_score(),
137	            metric=metric,
138	            num_samples=agent_result.num_scored(),
139	            per_sample=agent_result.per_sample() or None,
140	            stats=agent_result.token_totals(),
141	            turns=agent_result.total_turns(),
142	        )
143	
144	
145	@dataclass
146	class EvalResult:
147	    """Aggregated result of evaluating a model across one or more benchmarks."""
148	
149	    model: str
150	    backend: str
151	    benchmarks: dict[str, BenchmarkResult] = field(default_factory=dict)
152	    commands: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # exact eval commands executed
153	    healed: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)     # self-heal mutations applied
154	
155	    def add(self, result: BenchmarkResult) -> None:
156	        self.benchmarks[result.name] = result
157	        cmd = getattr(result, "command", "")
158	        if cmd and cmd not in self.commands:
159	            self.commands.append(cmd)
160	
161	    def mean_score(self) -> float:
162	        if not self.benchmarks:
163	            return 0.0
164	        return sum(b.score for b in self.benchmarks.values()) / len(self.benchmarks)
165	
166	    def efficiency(self) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
167	        """Token + turn totals across agentic benchmarks (``None`` if none carry any).
168	
169	        Only benchmarks produced by an agent (which attach a ``stats``/``turns``)
170	        contribute; a pure lm_eval run has no such provenance and yields ``None``.
171	        """
172	        from ..agent_eval.stats import TokenStats
173	
174	        tokens = TokenStats()
175	        total_turns = 0
176	        contributing = 0
177	        for b in self.benchmarks.values():
178	            if b.stats is not None:
179	                tokens.merge(b.stats)
180	            if b.turns:
181	                total_turns += b.turns
182	            if b.stats is not None or b.turns:
183	                contributing += 1
184	        if contributing == 0:
185	            return None
186	        eff: dict[str, Any] = {
187	            "num_benchmarks": contributing,
188	            "total_turns": total_turns,
189	        }
190	        if not tokens.is_empty():
191	            eff["tokens"] = tokens.to_dict()
192	        return eff
193	
194	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
195	        out: dict[str, Any] = {
196	            "model": self.model,
197	            "backend": self.backend,
198	            "mean_score": self.mean_score(),
199	            "results": {
200	                name: {"score": b.score, "metric": b.metric, "num_samples": b.num_samples}
201	                for name, b in self.benchmarks.items()
202	            },
203	            "commands": list(self.commands),
204	            "healed": list(self.healed),
205	        }
206	        eff = self.efficiency()
207	        if eff is not None:
208	            out["efficiency"] = eff
209	        return out
210	
211	
212	class BenchmarkRegistry:
213	    """Loads benchmark recipes from a directory (default: repo ``recipes/benchmarks``)."""
214	
215	    def __init__(self, root: Path | None = None):
216	        self.root = Path(root) if root else _RECIPE_ROOT
217	        self._cache: dict[str, BenchmarkRecipe] = {}
218	
219	    def _load_file(self, path: Path) -> BenchmarkRecipe:
220	        data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text()) or {}
221	        try:
222	            return BenchmarkRecipe.model_validate(data)
223	        except Exception as exc:
224	            raise RecipeError(f"invalid benchmark recipe {path}: {exc}") from exc
225

"""
Evaluate generated images using Mask2Former (or other object detector model)
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time

import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from PIL import Image, ImageOps
import torch
import mmdet
from mmdet.apis import inference_detector, init_detector

import open_clip
from clip_benchmark.metrics import zeroshot_classification as zsc
zsc.tqdm = lambda it, *args, **kwargs: it

# Get directory path

def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("imagedir", type=str)
    parser.add_argument("--outfile", type=str, default="results.jsonl")
    parser.add_argument("--model-config", type=str, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--model-path", type=str, default="./")
    # Other arguments
    parser.add_argument("--options", nargs="*", type=str, default=[])
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.options = dict(opt.split("=", 1) for opt in args.options)
    if args.model_config is None:
        args.model_config = os.path.join(
            os.path.dirname(mmdet.__file__),
            "../configs/mask2former/mask2former_swin-s-p4-w7-224_lsj_8x2_50e_coco.py"
        )
    return args

DEVICE = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
assert DEVICE == "cuda"

def timed(fn):
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        startt = time.time()
        result = fn(*args, **kwargs)
        endt = time.time()
        print(f'Function {fn.__name__!r} executed in {endt - startt:.3f}s', file=sys.stderr)
        return result
    return wrapper

# Load models

@timed
def load_models(args):
    CONFIG_PATH = args.model_config
    OBJECT_DETECTOR = args.options.get('model', "mask2former_swin-s-p4-w7-224_lsj_8x2_50e_coco")
    CKPT_PATH = os.path.join(args.model_path, f"{OBJECT_DETECTOR}.pth")
    object_detector = init_detector(CONFIG_PATH, CKPT_PATH, device=DEVICE)

    clip_arch = args.options.get('clip_model', "ViT-L-14")
    clip_model, _, transform = open_clip.create_model_and_transforms(clip_arch, pretrained="openai", device=DEVICE)
    tokenizer = open_clip.get_tokenizer(clip_arch)

    with open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "object_names.txt")) as cls_file:
        classnames = [line.strip() for line in cls_file]

    return object_detector, (clip_model, transform, tokenizer), classnames


COLORS = ["red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "purple", "pink", "brown", "black", "white"]
COLOR_CLASSIFIERS = {}

# Evaluation parts

class ImageCrops(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
    def __init__(self, image: Image.Image, objects):
        self._image = image.convert("RGB")
        bgcolor = args.options.get('bgcolor', "#999")
        if bgcolor == "original":
            self._blank = self._image.copy()
        else:
            self._blank = Image.new("RGB", image.size, color=bgcolor)
        self._objects = objects

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self._objects)

    def __getitem__(self, index):
        box, mask = self._objects[index]
        if mask is not None:
            assert tuple(self._image.size[::-1]) == tuple(mask.shape), (index, self._image.size[::-1], mask.shape)
            image = Image.composite(self._image, self._blank, Image.fromarray(mask))
        else:
            image = self._image
        if args.options.get('crop', '1') == '1':
            image = image.crop(box[:4])
        # if args.save:
        #     base_count = len(os.listdir(args.save))
        #     image.save(os.path.join(args.save, f"cropped_{base_count:05}.png"))
        return (transform(image), 0)


def color_classification(image, bboxes, classname):
    if classname not in COLOR_CLASSIFIERS:
        COLOR_CLASSIFIERS[classname] = zsc.zero_shot_classifier(
            clip_model, tokenizer, COLORS,
            [
                f"a photo of a {{c}} {classname}",
                f"a photo of a {{c}}-colored {classname}",
                f"a photo of a {{c}} object"
            ],
            DEVICE
        )
    clf = COLOR_CLASSIFIERS[classname]
    dataloader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(
        ImageCrops(image, bboxes),
        batch_size=16, num_workers=4
    )
    with torch.no_grad():
        pred, _ = zsc.run_classification(clip_model, clf, dataloader, DEVICE)
        return [COLORS[index.item()] for index in pred.argmax(1)]


def compute_iou(box_a, box_b):
    area_fn = lambda box: max(box[2] - box[0] + 1, 0) * max(box[3] - box[1] + 1, 0)
    i_area = area_fn([
        max(box_a[0], box_b[0]), max(box_a[1], box_b[1]),
        min(box_a[2], box_b[2]), min(box_a[3], box_b[3])
    ])
    u_area = area_fn(box_a) + area_fn(box_b) - i_area
    return i_area / u_area if u_area else 0


def relative_position(obj_a, obj_b):
    """Give position of A relative to B, factoring in object dimensions"""
    boxes = np.array([obj_a[0], obj_b[0]])[:, :4].reshape(2, 2, 2)
    center_a, center_b = boxes.mean(axis=-2)
    dim_a, dim_b = np.abs(np.diff(boxes, axis=-2))[..., 0, :]
    offset = center_a - center_b
    #
    revised_offset = np.maximum(np.abs(offset) - POSITION_THRESHOLD * (dim_a + dim_b), 0) * np.sign(offset)
    if np.all(np.abs(revised_offset) < 1e-3):
        return set()
    #
    dx, dy = revised_offset / np.linalg.norm(offset)
    relations = set()
    if dx < -0.5: relations.add("left of")
    if dx > 0.5: relations.add("right of")
    if dy < -0.5: relations.add("above")
    if dy > 0.5: relations.add("below")
    return relations


def evaluate(image, objects, metadata):
    """
    Evaluate given image using detected objects on the global metadata specifications.
    Assumptions:

def relative_position(obj_a, obj_b, position_threshold=POSITION_THRESHOLD):
    """Give position of A relative to B, factoring in object dimensions."""
    ax0, ay0, ax1, ay1 = obj_a[:4]
    bx0, by0, bx1, by1 = obj_b[:4]
    center_a = ((ax0 + ax1) / 2, (ay0 + ay1) / 2)
    center_b = ((bx0 + bx1) / 2, (by0 + by1) / 2)
    dim_a = (abs(ax1 - ax0), abs(ay1 - ay0))
    dim_b = (abs(bx1 - bx0), abs(by1 - by0))
    offset = (center_a[0] - center_b[0], center_a[1] - center_b[1])
    # dead-zone: shrink the offset by POSITION_THRESHOLD * (dim_a + dim_b)
    revised = tuple(
        max(abs(o) - position_threshold * (da + db), 0) * (1 if o > 0 else -1 if o < 0 else 0)
        for o, da, db in zip(offset, dim_a, dim_b)
    )
    if abs(revised[0]) < 1e-3 and abs(revised[1]) < 1e-3:
        return set()
    norm = math.hypot(*offset)
    dx, dy = revised[0] / norm, revised[1] / norm
    relations = set()
    if dx < -0.5: relations.add("left of")
    if dx > 0.5: relations.add("right of")
    if dy < -0.5: relations.add("above")
    if dy > 0.5: relations.add("below")
    return relations

def summarize(rows: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Port of summary_scores.py: per-tag mean of correct; overall = mean of task means."""
    by_tag = {}  # ordered by first appearance (groupby sort=False)
    for row in rows: by_tag.setdefault(row["tag"], []).append(bool(row["correct"]))
    task_means = {tag: sum(v)/len(v) for tag, v in by_tag.items()}
    overall = sum(task_means.values()) / len(task_means) if task_means else 0.0
    return {"task_means": task_means, "overall": overall, "num_images": len(rows)}

def classify_colors(self, image, detections, classname):
    # detections: [(box, mask), ...] in score order (already top-count)
    if not detections: return []
    weights = self._color_weights(classname)  # cached

    pred = logits.argmax(dim=-1)
    return [COLORS[i] for i in pred.tolist()]

{"content": """"GenEval benchmark: detection-based text-to-image alignment scoring.

Port of djghosh13/geneval's ``evaluation/evaluate_images.py`` +
``summary_scores.py`` (MIT, (c) 2023 Dhruba Ghosh -- see NOTICE; vendored
prompts/classes live in ``recipes/data/geneval/``).  The one deliberate
substitution: the official Mask2Former runs via mmdet; we use transformers'
``Mask2FormerForUniversalSegmentation`` instead (no mmdet dependency).  Its
instance post-processing yields per-segment masks + scores but *no boxes*, so
boxes are derived as mask bounding rects -- everything downstream (IoU
dedup, relative position, masked color crops) then matches the official math.

Official pipeline per image: per class keep detections with score >
``THRESHOLD`` (``COUNTING_THRESHOLD`` for the counting tag), cap at
``MAX_OBJECTS`` sorted by score, drop exact-duplicate boxes (IoU == 1.0);
``include`` clauses are AND-ed (count / zero-shot CLIP color on masked crops /
relative position), ``exclude`` clauses OR-ed.  Aggregation: per-tag mean of
per-image correctness, overall = unweighted mean of the six task means.

Heavy deps (torch / transformers / PIL / numpy) import lazily so the pure
scoring logic (IoU, position, evaluate, summarize) stays unit-testable without
a GPU stack.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from ..logging_util import AqaError, get_logger

_log = get_logger("eval.geneval")

# Repo-vendored official data (prompts/evaluation_metadata.jsonl +
# evaluation/object_names.txt from djghosh13/geneval).
DATA_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "recipes" / "data" / "geneval"

DEFAULT_DETECTOR = "facebook/mask2former-swin-small-coco-instance"
DEFAULT_CLIP_MODEL = "openai/clip-vit-large-patch14"

# Official options (evaluate_images.py defaults).
THRESHOLD = 0.3
COUNTING_THRESHOLD = 0.9
MAX_OBJECTS = 16
NMS_THRESHOLD = 1.0  # only exact (IoU == 1.0) duplicates are dropped
POSITION_THRESHOLD = 0.1

COLORS = [
    "red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue",
    "purple", "pink", "brown", "black", "white",
]
# Zero-shot color templates (official: classname substituted, {c} the color).
_COLOR_TEMPLATES = [
    "a photo of a {c} {classname}",
    "a photo of a {c}-colored {classname}",
    "a photo of a {c} object",
]

TASKS = ("single_object", "two_object", "counting", "colors", "position", "color_attr")


def load_classnames(data_dir: Path | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """The 80 COCO class names (vendored ``object_names.txt``), in order."""
    path = (data_dir or DATA_DIR) / "object_names.txt"
    return [line.strip() for line in path.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]


# ── pure geometry (ported verbatim in behavior) ──────────────────────────────
def compute_iou(box_a, box_b) -> float:
    """IoU of two ``[x0, y0, x1, y1, ...]`` boxes (+1 pixel area convention)."""
    def area(box):
        return max(box[2] - box[0] + 1, 0) * max(box[3] - box[1] + 1, 0)

    inter = area([
        max(box_a[0], box_b[0]), max(box_a[1], box_b[1]),
        min(box_a[2], box_b[2]), min(box_a[3], box_b[3]),
    ])
    union = area(box_a) + area(box_b) - inter
    return inter / union if union else 0


def relative_position(obj_a, obj_b, *, position_threshold: float = POSITION_THRESHOLD) -> set[str]:
    """Position of A relative to B, factoring in object dimensions.

    Port of the official rule: shrink the center offset by
    ``POSITION_THRESHOLD * (dim_a + dim_b)`` per axis (dead-zone -> no
    relation), then normalise by the *original* offset norm; |dx|/|dy| beyond
    0.5 select left/right and above/below.
    """
    boxes = [obj_a[:4], obj_b[:4]]
    center_a = ((boxes[0][0] + boxes[0][2]) / 2, (boxes[0][1] + boxes[0][3]) / 2)
    center_b = ((boxes[1][0] + boxes[1][2]) / 2, (boxes[1][1] + boxes[1][3]) / 2)
    dim_a = (abs(boxes[0][2] - boxes[0][0]), abs(boxes[0][3] - boxes[0][1]))
    dim_b = (abs(boxes[1][2] - boxes[1][0]), abs(boxes[1][3] - boxes[1][1]))
    offset = (center_a[0] - center_b[0], center_a[1] - center_b[1])
    revised = tuple(
        max(abs(o) - position_threshold * (da + db), 0.0) * (1.0 if o > 0 else -1.0 if o < 0 else 0.0)
        for o, da, db in zip(offset, dim_a, dim_b)
    )
    if all(abs(r) < 1e-3 for r in revised):
        return set()
    norm = math.hypot(*offset)
    dx, dy = revised[0] / norm, revised[1] / norm
    relations = set()
    if dx < -0.5:
        relations.add("left of")
    if dx > 0.5:
        relations.add("right of")
    if dy < -0.5:
        relations.add("above")
    if dy > 0.5:
        relations.add("below")
    return relations


def filter_detections(
    per_class: dict[str, list],
    *,
    threshold: float = THRESHOLD,
    max_objects: int = MAX_OBJECTS,
    nms_threshold: float = NMS_THRESHOLD,
) -> dict[str, list]:
    """Threshold -> sort by score desc -> cap -> drop exact duplicates.

    ``per_class`` maps a class name to raw ``([x0, y0, x1, y1, score], mask)``
    detections.  Mirrors the per-class filtering of the official
    ``evaluate_image`` (score strictly greater than the threshold; cap applied
    before dedup; with the default ``NMS_THRESHOLD == 1.0`` only boxes with
    IoU == 1.0 against an already-kept box are dropped).
    """
    detected: dict[str, list] = {}
    for classname, dets in per_class.items():
        dets = sorted(
            (d for d in dets if d[0][4] > threshold),
            key=lambda d: d[0][4], reverse=True,
        )[:max_objects]
        kept = []
        for det in dets:
            if all(compute_iou(det[0], prev[0]) < nms_threshold for prev in kept):
                kept.append(det)
        if kept:
            detected[classname] = kept
    return detected


# ── include/exclude evaluation (ported) ──────────────────────────────────────
def evaluate(
    image,
    objects: dict[str, list],
    metadata: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    classify_color,
    position_threshold: float = POSITION_THRESHOLD,
) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Evaluate detected ``objects`` against the prompt's ``metadata``.

    ``classify_color(image, detections, classname) -> list[str]`` is the
    zero-shot color classifier (CLIP-backed in production, faked in tests).
    Assumptions match upstream: include clauses combine with AND, exclude with
    OR; color/position only run on the most confident (top-``count``) objects.
    """
    correct = True
    reason = []
    matched_groups: list[list | None] = []
    for req in metadata.get("include", []):
        classname = req["class"]
        matched = True
        found_objects = objects.get(classname, [])[: req["count"]]
        if len(found_objects) < req["count"]:
            correct = matched = False
            reason.append(f"expected {classname}>={req['count']}, found {len(found_objects)}")
        else:
            if "color" in req:
                colors = classify_color(image, found_objects, classname)
                if colors.count(req["color"]) < req["count"]:
                    correct = matched = False
                    reason.append(
                        f"expected {req['color']} {classname}>={req['count']}, found "
                        f"{colors.count(req['color'])} {req['color']}; and "
                        + ", ".join(f"{colors.count(c)} {c}" for c in COLORS if c in colors)
                    )
            if "position" in req and matched:
                expected_rel, target_group = req["position"]
                if matched_groups[target_group] is None:
                    correct = matched = False
                    reason.append(f"no target for {classname} to be {expected_rel}")
                else:
                    for obj in found_objects:
                        for target_obj in matched_groups[target_group]:
                            true_rels = relative_position(
                                obj[0], target_obj[0], position_threshold=position_threshold
                            )
                            if expected_rel not in true_rels:
                                correct = matched = False
                                reason.append(
                                    f"expected {classname} {expected_rel} target, found "
                                    f"{' and '.join(true_rels)} target"
                                )
                                break
                        if not matched:
                            break
        matched_groups.append(found_objects if matched else None)
    for req in metadata.get("exclude", []):
        classname = req["class"]
        if len(objects.get(classname, [])) >= req["count"]:
            correct = False
            reason.append(
                f"expected {classname}<{req['count']}, found {len(objects[classname])}"
            )
    return correct, "\n".join(reason)


# ── aggregation (summary_scores.py port) ─────────────────────────────────────
def summarize(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Per-tag mean of per-image correctness; overall = unweighted task mean."""
    by_tag: dict[str, list[bool]] = {}
    for row in rows:
        by_tag.setdefault(row["tag"], []).append(bool(row["correct"]))
    task_means = {tag: sum(vals) / len(vals) for tag, vals in by_tag.items()}
    overall = sum(task_means.values()) / len(task_means) if task_means else 0.0
    return {"overall": overall, "task_means": task_means, "num_images": len(rows)}


# ── detector + CLIP-backed scorer ────────────────────────────────────────────
class GenevalScorer:
    """Mask2Former detection + CLIP color classification over generated images.

    Models load lazily on first use so constructing the scorer (and importing
    this module) stays cheap and GPU-free; tests inject fakes by monkeypatching
    :meth:`detect` / :meth:`classify_colors`.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        detector_model: str = DEFAULT_DETECTOR,
        clip_model: str = DEFAULT_CLIP_MODEL,
        device: str = "auto",
        data_dir: str | Path | None = None,
        threshold: float = THRESHOLD,
        counting_threshold: float = COUNTING_THRESHOLD,
        max_objects: int = MAX_OBJECTS,
        nms_threshold: float = NMS_THRESHOLD,
        position_threshold: float = POSITION_THRESHOLD,
    ):
        self.detector_model = detector_model
        self.clip_model = clip_model
        self.device = device
        self.data_dir = Path(data_dir) if data_dir else DATA_DIR
        self.threshold = threshold
        self.counting_threshold = counting_threshold
        self.max_objects = max_objects
        self.nms_threshold = nms_threshold
        self.position_threshold = position_threshold
        self.classnames = load_classnames(self.data_dir)
        self._detector = None
        self._det_processor = None
        self._clip = None
        self._clip_processor = None
        self._color_classifiers: dict[str, Any] = {}

    # -- lazy model loading --------------------------------------------------
    def _resolve_device(self) -> str:
        if self.device != "auto":
            return self.device
        import torch

        return "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

    def _load_detector(self):
        if self._detector is not None:
            return
        try:
            import torch  # noqa: F401
            from transformers import AutoImageProcessor, Mask2FormerForUniversalSegmentation
        except ImportError as exc:
            raise AqaError(
                "geneval scoring needs torch + transformers: pip install transformers torch"
            ) from exc
        device = self._resolve_device()
        self._detector = Mask2FormerForUniversalSegmentation.from_pretrained(
            self.detector_model
        ).to(device)
        self._detector.eval()
        self._det_processor = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained(self.detector_model)

    def _load_clip(self):
        if self._clip is not None:
            return
        try:
            import torch  # noqa: F401
            from transformers import CLIPModel, CLIPProcessor
        except ImportError as exc:
            raise AqaError(
                "geneval color scoring needs torch + transformers: pip install transformers torch"
            ) from exc
        device = self._resolve_device()
        self._clip = CLIPModel.from_pretrained(self.clip_model).to(device)
        self._clip.eval()
        self._clip_processor = CLIPProcessor.from_pretrained(self.clip_model)

    # -- detection -----------------------------------------------------------
    def _classname_for(self, label_id: int) -> str | None:
        """Map a detector label id to the vendored COCO class name."""
        id2label = getattr(self._detector.config, "id2label", None) or {}
        name = id2label.get(label_id, id2label.get(str(label_id)))
        if name is None and 0 <= label_id < len(self.classnames):
            name = self.classnames[label_id]
        return name if name in set(self.classnames) else None

    def detect(self, filepath) -> tuple[Any, dict[str, list]]:
        """Run the detector; return ``(image, detected)`` (filtered per class).

        transformers' instance post-processing returns a segmentation map plus
        per-segment ``(id, label_id, score)`` but no boxes, so each box is the
        segment mask's bounding rect with the segment score appended --
        the ``[x0, y0, x1, y1, score]`` shape the official mmdet path has.
        """
        self._load_detector()
        import torch
        from PIL import Image, ImageOps

        image = ImageOps.exif_transpose(Image.open(filepath))
        inputs = self._det_processor(images=image, return_tensors="pt").to(
            self._resolve_device()
        )
        with torch.no_grad():
            outputs = self._detector(**inputs)
        result = self._det_processor.post_process_instance_segmentation(
            outputs, threshold=0.0, target_sizes=[image.size[::-1]]
        )[0]
        segmentation = result["segmentation"]
        per_class: dict[str, list] = {}
        for seg in result["segments_info"]:
            classname = self._classname_for(seg["label_id"])
            if classname is None:
                continue
            mask = segmentation == seg["id"]
            ys, xs = mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
            if xs.numel() == 0:
                continue
            score = float(seg.get("score", 1.0))
            box = [xs.min().item(), ys.min().item(), xs.max().item(), ys.max().item(), score]
            per_class.setdefault(classname, []).append((box, mask))
        # official: counting tag uses the stricter confidence threshold
        threshold = self.threshold  # caller's tag-specific choice happens in evaluate_image
        return image, per_class, threshold

    # -- zero-shot color classification (CLIP) --------------------------------
    def _color_weights(self, classname: str):
        """Normalized mean text embedding per color (cached per classname)."""
        if classname in self._color_classifiers:
            return self._color_classifiers[classname]
        self._load_clip()
        import torch

        templates = [t.replace("{classname}", classname) for t in _COLOR_TEMPLATES]
        embs = []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for color in COLORS:
                texts = [t.format(c=color) for t in templates]
                inputs = self._clip_processor(
                    text=texts, return_tensors="pt", padding=True, truncation=True
                ).to(self._resolve_device())
                feats = self._clip.get_text_features(**inputs)
                feats = feats / feats.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
                embs.append(feats.mean(dim=0))
        weights = torch.stack(embs)
        weights = weights / weights.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        self._color_classifiers[classname] = weights
        return weights

    @staticmethod
    def _masked_crop(image, box, mask):
        """Composite the object on a #999 background by its mask, then crop."""
        from PIL import Image

        if mask is not None:
            blank = Image.new("RGB", image.size, color="#999")
            image = Image.composite(image, blank, Image.fromarray(mask))
        return image.crop(box[:4])

    def classify_colors(self, image, detections, classname: str) -> list[str]:
        """Zero-shot color label per detection (score-sorted) via CLIP."""
        if not detections:
            return []
        self._load_clip()
        import torch

        weights = self._color_weights(classname)
        crops = [self._masked_crop(image, box, mask) for box, mask in detections]
        inputs = self._clip_processor(images=crops, return_tensors="pt").to(
            self._resolve_device()
        )
        with torch.no_grad():
            feats = self._clip.get_image_features(**inputs)
        feats = feats / feats.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        pred = (feats @ weights.T).argmax(dim=-1)
        return [COLORS[i] for i in pred.tolist()]

    # -- per-image / per-directory evaluation ---------------------------------
    def evaluate_image(self, filepath, metadata: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Score one image; returns the official results.jsonl row shape."""
        image, per_class, _ = self.detect(filepath)
        # counting prompts use the stricter confidence threshold
        threshold = (
            self.counting_threshold if metadata["tag"] == "counting" else self.threshold
        )
        detected = filter_detections(
            per_class, threshold=threshold, max_objects=self.max_objects,
            nms_threshold=self.nms_threshold,
        )
        is_correct, reason = evaluate(
            image, detected, metadata,
            classify_color=self.classify_colors,
            position_threshold=self.position_threshold,
        )
        return {
            "filename": str(filepath),
            "tag": metadata["tag"],
            "prompt": metadata["prompt"],
            "correct": is_correct,
            "reason": reason,
            "metadata": json.dumps(metadata),
            "details": json.dumps({
                key: [list(map(float, box)) for box, _ in value]
                for key, value in detected.items()
            }),
        }

    def evaluate_directory(self, imagedir: str | Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Score an official-layout image dir (``<idx>/metadata.jsonl`` +
        ``<idx>/samples/<j>.png``); port of the official ``main()`` walk."""
        imagedir = Path(imagedir)
        results = []
        for folderpath in sorted(imagedir.iterdir()):
            if not folderpath.is_dir() or not folderpath.name.isdigit():
                continue
            metadata = json.loads((folderpath / "metadata.jsonl").read_text())
            samples = folderpath / "samples"
            for imagepath in sorted(samples.iterdir()):
                if not imagepath.is_file() or not re.match(r"\d+\.png", imagepath.name):
                    continue
                results.append(self.evaluate_image(imagepath, metadata))
        return results

    def write_results(self, rows: list[dict[str, Any]], outfile: str | Path) -> Path:
        """Write rows as results.jsonl (same shape as the official tool)."""
        outfile = Path(outfile)
        outfile.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        outfile.write_text(
            "".join(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n" for r in rows)
        )
        return outfile

from aqa.eval.registry import BenchmarkRegistry
from aqa.logging_util import AqaError


def _det(x0, y0, x1, y1, score):
    """A ([x0, y0, x1, y1, score], mask) detection (mask unused by the logic)."""
    return ([x0, y0, x1, y1, score], None)


def _meta(tag, include, exclude=None, prompt="p"):
    m = {"tag": tag, "include": include, "prompt": prompt}
    if exclude:
        m["exclude"] = exclude
    return m


def _classify(colors_by_class):
    """Fake zero-shot color classifier: scripted colors per classname."""
    def classify(image, detections, classname):
        return list(colors_by_class.get(classname, []))[: len(detections)]

    return classify


# ── geometry ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def test_compute_iou():
    box = [0, 0, 10, 10, 0.9]
    assert compute_iou(box, box) == 1.0
    assert compute_iou(box, [100, 100, 110, 110, 0.5]) == 0.0
    # +1 pixel area convention: [0,0,1,1] vs [1,1,2,2] share exactly one pixel
    assert compute_iou([0, 0, 1, 1], [1, 1, 2, 2]) == pytest.approx(1 / 7)


def test_relative_position_cardinals_and_dead_zone():
    a = [0, 0, 10, 10]
    b = [100, 0, 110, 10]
    assert relative_position(a, b) == {"left of"}
    assert relative_position(b, a) == {"right of"}
    assert relative_position([0, 0, 10, 10], [0, 100, 10, 110]) == {"above"}
    assert relative_position([0, 100, 10, 110], [0, 0, 10, 10]) == {"below"}
    # diagonal: both relations
    assert relative_position([0, 0, 10, 10], [100, 100, 110, 110]) == {"left of", "above"}
    # dead zone: same center -> no relation
    assert relative_position([0, 0, 10, 10], [5, 0, 15, 10]) == set()
    # the shrunk offset crossing no 0.5 threshold -> no relation
    # centers 50 apart, dims shrink the offset to exactly the -0.5 boundary
    assert relative_position([0, 0, 100, 100], [90, 0, 190, 100]) == set()


def test_relative_position_threshold_shrinks_by_dimensions():
    # offset 40, dims sum 200 -> revised 40 - 0.1*200 = 20, norm 40 -> dx = -0.5
    assert relative_position([0, 0, 100, 100], [40, 0, 140, 100]) == set()
    # a wider gap clears the boundary
    assert relative_position([0, 0, 100, 100], [200, 0, 300, 100]) == {"left of"}


# ── detection filtering ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def test_filter_detections_threshold_is_strict():
    dets = {"dog": [_det(0, 0, 5, 5, 0.3), _det(0, 0, 5, 5, 0.31)]}
    out = filter_detections(dets, threshold=0.3)
    # score == threshold is dropped (official uses strictly-greater)
    assert len(out["dog"]) == 1 and out["dog"][0][0][4] == pytest.approx(0.31)


def test_filter_detections_counting_threshold():
    dets = {"clock": [_det(0, 0, 5, 5, 0.85), _det(10, 0, 15, 5, 0.95)]}
    assert "clock" in filter_detections(dets, threshold=THRESHOLD)  # 0.85 passes 0.3
    out = filter_detections(dets, threshold=COUNTING_THRESHOLD)
    assert len(out["clock"]) == 1 and out["clock"][0][0][4] == 0.95  # 0.85 dropped at 0.9


def test_filter_detections_sort_cap_and_exact_dup_dedup():
    dets = [_det(i, 0, i + 5, 5, 0.5 + i * 0.01) for i in range(MAX_OBJECTS + 2)]
    out = filter_detections({"dog": dets})
    assert len(out["dog"]) == MAX_OBJECTS
    scores = [d[0][4] for d in out["dog"]]
    assert scores == sorted(scores, reverse=True)
    # identical boxes (IoU == 1.0) are deduped; near-duplicates are kept
    dup = [_det(0, 0, 5, 5, 0.9), _det(0, 0, 5, 5, 0.8), _det(0, 0, 6, 5, 0.7)]
    out = filter_detections({"dog": dup})
    assert [d[0][4] for d in out["dog"]] == [0.9, 0.7]


# ── include/exclude evaluation per tag ───────────────────────────────────────
def test_evaluate_single_object():
    meta = _meta("single_object", [{"class": "dog", "count": 1}])
    ok, reason = evaluate(None, {"dog": [_det(0, 0, 5, 5, 0.9)]}, meta,
                          classify_color=_classify({}))
    assert ok and reason == ""
    ok, reason = evaluate(None, {}, meta, classify_color=_classify({}))
    assert not ok and "expected dog>=1, found 0" in reason


def test_evaluate_two_object_multi_include():
    meta = _meta("two_object", [{"class": "dog", "count": 1}, {"class": "cat", "count": 1}])
    objects = {"dog": [_det(0, 0, 5, 5, 0.9)], "cat": [_det(10, 0, 15, 5, 0.8)]}
    assert evaluate(None, objects, meta, classify_color=_classify({}))[0]
    # one include missing -> the whole AND fails
    assert not evaluate(None, {"dog": objects["dog"]}, meta, classify_color=_classify({}))[0]


def test_evaluate_counting_include_and_exclude():
    meta = _meta("counting", [{"class": "clock", "count": 2}],
                 exclude=[{"class": "clock", "count": 3}])
    clocks = [_det(i * 10, 0, i * 10 + 5, 5, 0.95) for i in range(3)]
    assert evaluate(None, {"clock": clocks[:2]}, meta, classify_color=_classify({}))[0]
    ok, reason = evaluate(None, {"clock": clocks[:1]}, meta, classify_color=_classify({}))
    assert not ok and "expected clock>=2, found 1" in reason
    ok, reason = evaluate(None, {"clock": clocks}, meta, classify_color=_classify({}))
    assert not ok and "expected clock<3, found 3" in reason  # exclude triggers


def test_evaluate_colors_uses_classifier():
    meta = _meta("colors", [{"class": "fire hydrant", "count": 1, "color": "blue"}])
    objects = {"fire hydrant": [_det(0, 0, 5, 5, 0.9)]}
    ok, _ = evaluate(None, objects, meta,
                     classify_color=_classify({"fire hydrant": ["blue"]}))
    assert ok
    ok, reason = evaluate(None, objects, meta,
                          classify_color=_classify({"fire hydrant": ["red"]}))
    assert not ok and "expected blue fire hydrant>=1, found 0 blue" in reason


def test_evaluate_position_against_group_zero():
    # official shape: dog positioned relative to include-group 0 (teddy bear)
    meta = _meta("position", [{"class": "teddy bear", "count": 1},
                              {"class": "dog", "count": 1, "position": ["right of", 0]}])
    bear = {"teddy bear": [_det(0, 0, 10, 10, 0.9)]}
    dog_right = {"dog": [_det(100, 0, 110, 10, 0.9)]}
    ok, _ = evaluate(None, {**bear, **dog_right}, meta, classify_color=_classify({}))
    assert ok
    dog_left = {"dog": [_det(-100, 0, -90, 10, 0.9)]}
    ok, reason = evaluate(None, {**bear, **dog_left}, meta, classify_color=_classify({}))
    assert not ok and "expected dog right of target" in reason
    # no target: group 0 unmatched -> position cannot be checked
    ok, reason = evaluate(None, dog_right, meta, classify_color=_classify({}))
    assert not ok
    assert "no target for dog to be right of" in reason


def test_evaluate_exclude_only():
    meta = _meta("single_object", [{"class": "dog", "count": 1}],
                 exclude=[{"class": "cat", "count": 1}])
    objects = {"dog": [_det(0, 0, 5, 5, 0.9)], "cat": [_det(10, 0, 15, 5, 0.8)]}
    ok, reason = evaluate(None, objects, meta, classify_color=_classify({}))
    assert not ok and "expected cat<1, found 1" in reason


# ── aggregation (summary_scores.py formula) ──────────────────────────────────
def test_summarize_is_unweighted_mean_of_task_means():
    rows = (
        [{"tag": "single_object", "correct": i == 0} for i in range(4)]  # mean 0.25
        + [{"tag": "colors", "correct": True}]                            # mean 1.0
    )
    summary = summarize(rows)
    assert summary["task_means"] == {"single_object": 0.25, "colors": 1.0}
    # unweighted mean of task means, NOT the global mean (2/5 = 0.4)
    assert summary["overall"] == pytest.approx(0.625)
    assert summary["num_images"] == 5

def _fake_scorer(monkeypatch, per_class, colors=None):
    scorer = GenevalScorer()
    monkeypatch.setattr(GenevalScorer, "detect",
                        lambda self, filepath: (None, per_class))
    if colors is not None:
        monkeypatch.setattr(GenevalScorer, "classify_colors",
                            lambda self, image, dets, classname: colors(dets, classname))
    return scorer

Boxes [0,0,10,10] and [5,0,15,10]: centers (5,5) vs (10,5) → offset (-5, 0); dims (10,10),(10,10) → shrink 0.1*20=2 → revised (-3, 0); norm(offset)=5 → dx=-0.6 < -0.5 → "left of". My test comment claimed dead zone but the math gives left of. The official semantics indeed give left of here. Fix the test: use truly degenerate cases:

Official: `revised_offset / np.linalg.norm(offset)` — if all revised < 1e-3 it returns set() BEFORE the division. Identical centers: offset (0,0), revised (0,0) → `np.all(np.abs(revised) < 1e-3)` → return set(). My port: `if all(abs(r) < 1e-3 ...) return set()` before division ✓. GenEval benchmark support implemented on top of the existing working tree — nothing reverted, no commits. Official logic was ported from the actual upstream sources ([evaluate_images.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/djghosh13/geneval/main/evaluation/evaluate_images.py) / [summary_scores.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/djghosh13/geneval/main/evaluation/summary_scores.py), fetched and read, not guessed).

## Files added

- **`aqa/eval/geneval.py`** — the scorer. Pure, GPU-free logic: `compute_iou` (+1 pixel area convention), `relative_position` (dead-zone shrink by `POSITION_THRESHOLD*(dim_a+dim_b)`, normalize by *original* offset norm, ±0.5 sign thresholds → left of/right of/above/below), `filter_detections` (strict `score > threshold`, sort desc, cap `MAX_OBJECTS=16`, drop IoU==1.0 duplicates), `evaluate` (include=AND with count/color/position clauses + `matched_groups` bookkeeping, exclude=OR, official reason strings), `summarize` (per-tag mean of per-image correct; **overall = unweighted mean of task means**). `GenevalScorer` loads models lazily: transformers `Mask2FormerForUniversalSegmentation` + `AutoImageProcessor` (default `facebook/mask2former-swin-small-coco-instance`) and CLIP ViT-L/14 (`openai/clip-vit-large-patch14`, 10 colors × 3 templates, mean+normalize text weights per classname, masked-crop compositing on `#999` then bbox crop — the `ImageCrops` port). `evaluate_image` returns the official `results.jsonl` row shape (`filename/tag/prompt/correct/reason/metadata/details`); `evaluate_directory` ports the official `<idx>/metadata.jsonl` + `<idx>/samples/<j>.png` walk (numeric dirs, `\d+\.png` regex); `write_results` emits diffable JSONL.
- **`recipes/data/geneval/evaluation_metadata.jsonl`** (553 official prompts, verified: 80 single_object / 99 two_object / 80 counting / 94 colors / 100 position / 100 color_attr) and **`object_names.txt`** (80 COCO classes) — downloaded byte-exact via curl from upstream @main.
- **`recipes/benchmarks/geneval.yaml`** — harness diffusion, `dataset: recipes/data/geneval/evaluation_metadata.jsonl` (repo-relative), `prompt_field: prompt`, `images_per_prompt: 4`, `scoring.scorer: geneval` with `detector_model`/`clip_model` knobs defaulted.
- **`tests/test_geneval.py`** (19 tests) — IoU/position/dead-zone geometry, strict-threshold + counting-0.9 + cap + exact-dup dedup filtering, per-tag evaluate paths (single/two/counting/colors/position incl. no-target and dead-zone, exclude, multi-include), official aggregation formula (0.625 unweighted vs 0.4 weighted fixture), scorer with monkeypatched `detect`/`classify_colors`, directory walk + results.jsonl round-trip, vendored classnames, recipe load + repo-relative dataset resolution from an unrelated cwd, empty-results `AqaError`.
- **`tests/test_diffusion_harness.py`** (+3 tests) — `images_per_prompt=2` official layout (metadata.jsonl per prompt, `samples/<j>.png`, 5-col metadata.csv, seeds `seed+idx*1000+j` = 42/43/1042/1043) + resume skips completed samples; `group_key` separation; geneval scoring dispatch (metric/score/per_sample/raw/command/results.jsonl).

## Files modified

- **`aqa/eval/registry.py`** — `BenchmarkRecipe.images_per_prompt: int = Field(default=1, ge=1)`; new `GenevalSpec` (`detector_model`/`clip_model` defaults) wired into `ScoringSpec.geneval` (all `extra="forbid"` preserved).
- **`aqa/eval/harness/diffusion.py`** — `_load_prompt_rows` extracted (raw rows; repo-root-relative fallback for local dataset paths so `recipes/data/...` works from any cwd), `_load_prompts` delegates; `_generate_images` splits into `_generate_single` (byte-identical legacy behavior) and `_generate_multi` (official layout, per-sample resume via `sample` column); shared `_generate_one`; `group_key` now includes `recipe.images_per_prompt` + `recipe.scoring.scorer`; `_result_for` dispatches `scoring.scorer == "geneval"` → `_result_geneval` (metric `geneval`, score=overall 0..1, `num_samples`=images evaluated, `per_sample`=per-image 0/1, `raw` = task_means + results path + model ids); `_command_str` takes an optional scorer description so the reproducibility string records the geneval stack. CLIP path untouched.
- **`NOTICE`** — GenEval attribution: MIT, (c) 2023 Dhruba Ghosh, github.com/djghosh13/geneval (vendored data + scoring-logic port noted).

## Verification

- `~/.venv-aqa-test/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q` → **482 passed** (baseline **460**; +22 new). Existing swebench/diffusion/local-env/traces tests all still green.
- `~/.venv-aqa-test/bin/python -m ruff check aqa/ tests/` → **All checks passed!**

## Deviations

1. **transformers Mask2Former has no boxes**: `post_process_instance_segmentation` returns a segmentation map + `segments_info` (`id/label_id/score`) but no bboxes (mmdet returns box arrays). Boxes are therefore derived as each segment mask's bounding rect (`nonzero` min/max, `+score` appended) — the only structural approximation vs mmdet; all downstream math (IoU, position, crops) is then identical. Label mapping goes through `model.config.id2label` intersected with the vendored `object_names.txt` set (fallback: index into the vendored list).
2. **NMS at `NMS_THRESHOLD == 1.0`**: upstream *short-circuits* and keeps even exact duplicates; per your spec ("drops IoU==1.0 duplicates") I drop boxes with IoU == 1.0 against a kept box. Identical behavior for every non-identical box pair.
3. **CLIP via transformers instead of open_clip**: same math (per-color mean of the 3 template embeddings, L2-normalized, argmax of normalized image-feature dot product); the scalar logit scale is ranking-invariant so it's omitted. The official's `num_workers=4` DataLoader is replaced by a single batched processor call (no behavioral difference, simpler).
4. **Processor threshold set to 0.0** so the harness's own per-tag thresholds (0.3 / 0.9 counting) do the filtering exactly like upstream, rather than letting transformers pre-filter.
5. **`evaluate_directory` returns `[]` for a missing image dir** (upstream crashes with `os.listdir`); the harness converts that into a clean `AqaError("geneval: no generated images …")`.

## 4. 里程碑与验收

| 里程碑 | 内容 | 验收 |
|---|---|---|
| **M-A 卫生与基础**（约 1 周，可立即开始） | P0 卫生债（对标文档 §6.1–6.3）+ D1 recipe_store 闭环 + D2 scheme 校验 + D9 recipe CI | 全量测试绿；同模型二次 run 命中 pinned recipe；坏 recipe 被测试拦截 |
| **M-B 评估规模化**（2–3 周） | D3 外部 recipe 注入 + D4 自描述扩展 + D5 raw 落盘/rescore + D6 失败分类 + D7 repeats + D8 resume/分片 | 仓外 recipe 直接可跑；`aqa rescore` 离线重算一致；3-benchmark run 可 kill→resume；2 分片 merge 一致 |
| **M-C 量化深化**（与 M-B 并行，联动 diffusion plan M2/M3） | D10 gate 方向 + D11 部署冒烟 +（diffusion plan 已定项：Z-Image/FLUX.2、MXFP8、optimize DiT 分支） | 加载失败在 smoke 阶段以 infra_error 终止；diffusion 全链路含失败分类报告 |
| **M-D benchmark 迁移流水线**（M-B 地基之后；契约细节见 `nemo_skills_deep_dive.md`） | ① `module::Class` 动态定位（scorer/evaluator/metrics 三处注册表支持路径形式）；② 聚合算术移植（无偏 pass@k 组合数、majority@k tie-break、std_dev/std_err_across_runs → `report/stats.py`）；③ `math_verify` 判分接入 scorer 库；④ 按模型需求逐类迁移 benchmark：**竞赛数学（AIME24/25/26、OMNI-MATH）→ 代码（LiveCodeBench 时间切片/BigCodeBench，code_exec 沙箱承载）→ 长上下文（RULER 动态生成）→ 多语（mmlu-prox 等纯数据）→ check_contamination**；lm_eval 已覆盖的不迁 | 每个迁入的 benchmark：recipe yaml + scorer/evaluator + CI 校验测试 + 与上游公布口径的数值对齐记录 |
| **M-E 轨迹数据化**（借鉴 Harbor：ATIF 格式 + traces export，见 [harbor training-workflows](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/tree/main/docs/content/docs/training-workflows)） | ① `agent_eval` Trajectory → ATIF-v1.7 导出（`agent_eval/atif.py`）+ run 落盘 `trajectories.jsonl`；② `aqa traces export`：agent_eval 轨迹 → OpenAI messages / ShareGPT 数据集（success 过滤、parquet/HF push 可选）；③ fix-loop 修复轨迹（TrajectoryStore + KnowledgeStore patch）→ 正样本 SFT 数据集 | 单测覆盖转换/过滤/格式；真实 run 产出数据集并可用 Harbor `traces export` 交叉消费 |
| **M-F 可插拔相位 hooks（capability 组件层）** | 新增 `aqa.hooks` entry-point group + 有序 hook 链（`aqa/hooks/`）：`after_quantize` / `before_benchmark` / `after_benchmark` 等相位；validator 类 hook 可判死相位，其余 hook 出错只记日志。种子实现：`quant_sanity`（导出带 quantization_config 但无打包权重 → 判失败，实跑教训）、`eval_sanity`（全零分甄别，从 pipeline 内联逻辑迁入）。判断类能力走 skill 包（skills/、fix_playbook），机制类能力走 hooks——后续新能力（外部 harness 移植、trajectory 捕获、soft-fail 等）一律以 hook 形式注册 | hooks 协议 + 注册 + 两个种子 hook 的测试；`quant_sanity` 用今晚的 0 层事故做回归 fixture |
| **P2 平台化**（按需） | D12 各项 | 逐项立项时再定 |

## 5. 风险与取舍

1. **raw 落盘的体积**：`log_samples` 全量存 prompt+response，大套件下 GB 级——sink 上传默认排除 raw（manifest 记路径），本地保留。
2. **repeats 的成本**：N 倍推理成本，默认 1 不变；pass@k/majority@k 依赖 D5，分两期避免一次性大改。
3. **lm_eval 路径的能力上限**：raw 转存依赖 lm_eval 的 samples 输出格式，换版本可能破损——转存器做版本哨兵（字段缺失时降级为「无 raw」并 warning，不炸 run）。
4. **不引入 Hydra/NeMo-Run/Slurm**：aqa 的零依赖 config 组合器与 ssh+docker executor 已够现状；执行后端的规模化等真有集群需求时再立项。
5. **与 NeMo-Gym 的迁徙保持观察**：Skills 的 benchmark 正迁往 NeMo-Gym，NEL 用 `gym://`/`skills://` URI 接入——aqa 的 D3 目录注入已等价覆盖私有场景，URI scheme 集成（`lm-eval://` 等）暂不需要，因为 aqa 的 lm_eval harness 已是深度集成而非容器外壳。

68	def _load_target(target: str) -> Any:
69	    """Import a ``module:attr`` (or ``module.attr``) target string."""
70	    if ":" in target:
71	        module_name, _, attr = target.partition(":")
72	    else:
73	        module_name, _, attr = target.rpartition(".")
74	    module = importlib.import_module(module_name)

78	class Registry:
79	    """A named plugin group resolved from entry points + builtin fallbacks."""
80	
81	    def __init__(self, group: str):
82	        self.group = group
83	        self._extra: dict[str, str] = {}  # runtime registrations (tests / dynamic plugins)
84	
85	    def register(self, name: str, target: str) -> None:
86	        """Register (or override) ``name`` -> ``module:attr`` at runtime."""
87	        self._extra[name] = target
88	
89	    def _discover(self) -> dict[str, str]:
90	        table: dict[str, str] = dict(_BUILTINS.get(self.group, {}))
91	        try:
92	            eps = metadata.entry_points(group=self.group)
93	        except TypeError:  # pragma: no cover - very old importlib.metadata
94	            eps = metadata.entry_points().get(self.group, [])  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
95	        for ep in eps:
96	            table[ep.name] = ep.value
97	        table.update(self._extra)
98	        return table
99	
100	    def names(self) -> list[str]:
101	        return sorted(self._discover())
102	
103	    def get(self, name: str) -> Any:
104	        table = self._discover()
105	        if name not in table:
106	            raise RegistryError(
107	                f"unknown {self.group} plugin {name!r}; available: {', '.join(sorted(table)) or '<none>'}"
108	            )
109	        return _load_target(table[name])
110	
111	    def create(self, name: str, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
112	        """Resolve ``name`` and instantiate it (for class-based plugins)."""
113	        return self.get(name)(*args, **kwargs)

269	    """Evaluate, wrapping the phase in the agent fix-loop when enabled.
270	
271	    A phase is considered failed when the harness raises OR every benchmark scores
272	    exactly 0 (acc=0 => fail, matching the leaderboard's failure heuristic). On
273	    failure the fix-loop hands the agent the full traceback and lets it decide --
274	    there is no deterministic pre-pass.

from __future__ import annotations

from functools import lru_cache
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable

from ..logging_util import AqaError, get_logger
from ..registry import HOOKS

if TYPE_CHECKING: ...

DEFAULT_HOOKS = ("quant_sanity", "eval_sanity")

@runtime_checkable
class PhaseHook(Protocol):
    name: str
    def after_quantize(self, run_cfg, quant_cfg, output_dir) -> None: ...
    def after_benchmark(self, run_cfg, recipe, result_or_exception, out_dir) -> None: ...

@lru_cache(maxsize=8)
def _resolve(names: tuple[str, ...]) -> tuple:
    return tuple(HOOKS.create(n) for n in names)

def resolve_hooks(run_cfg) -> tuple:
    """The configured hook chain (resolved once per distinct config)."""
    names = DEFAULT_HOOKS if run_cfg.hooks is None else tuple(run_cfg.hooks)
    return _resolve(tuple(names))

def run_hook_chain(phase: str, chain, run_cfg=None, **ctx) -> None:
    for hook in chain or ():
        fn = getattr(hook, phase, None)
        if fn is None:
            continue
        _log.debug("hook %s.%s", getattr(hook, "name", hook), phase)
        try:
            fn(run_cfg, **ctx)
        except AqaError:
            raise  # validator semantics: the hook deliberately fails the phase
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - hooks never crash a run
            _log.warning("hook %s.%s failed (ignored): %s", getattr(hook, "name", hook), phase, exc)

def run_hooks(phase: str, run_cfg, **ctx) -> None:
    run_hook_chain(phase, resolve_hooks(run_cfg), run_cfg, **ctx)

    claiming = []

    for comp in _COMPONENT_DIRS:

{"content": """"Pluggable phase hooks (capability components).

A :class:`PhaseHook` is a named object with per-phase methods
(``after_quantize`` / ``after_benchmark``, ...).  Hooks are where
cross-cutting *mechanism* capabilities plug in -- validation, taxonomy,
trajectory capture, soft-fail policies -- so a new capability ships as a hook
registration instead of pipeline surgery.  (Judgment capabilities keep living
in the skill packages: ``skills/``, fix playbooks.)

Semantics:

* a hook raises :class:`~aqa.logging_util.AqaError` to deliberately FAIL the
  phase (validator semantics -- the error feeds the fix-loop's signature);
* any other exception inside a hook is caught, logged at WARNING, and never
  crashes the run;
* hooks run in configured order; every invocation is logged at DEBUG.

Registration mirrors the other extension points: the ``aqa.hooks``
entry-point group (pyproject) plus the builtin fallback map in
``aqa/registry.py``.  The active chain comes from ``run_cfg.hooks``:
``None`` => the built-in defaults, an explicit list => exactly those,
``[]`` => all hooks off.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from functools import lru_cache
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Protocol, runtime_checkable

from ..logging_util import AqaError, get_logger
from ..registry import HOOKS

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover
    from pathlib import Path

    from ..config import QuantConfig, RunConfig
    from ..eval.registry import BenchmarkRecipe

_log = get_logger("hooks")

# Hooks active when the run config does not name a chain explicitly.
DEFAULT_HOOKS = ("quant_sanity", "eval_sanity")


@runtime_checkable
class PhaseHook(Protocol):
    """A capability component invoked at phase boundaries.

    Implement only the phases you care about; the runner skips phases a hook
    does not define.  Raise ``AqaError`` to fail the phase on purpose.
    """

    name: str

    def after_quantize(
        self, run_cfg: RunConfig | None, quant_cfg: QuantConfig | None,
        output_dir: Path,
    ) -> None:
        """Runs after quantization + post-export repair, before eval."""
        ...

    def after_benchmark(
        self, run_cfg: RunConfig | None, recipe: BenchmarkRecipe,
        result_or_exception, out_dir: Path,
    ) -> None:
        """Runs per benchmark result as the evaluate phase assembles it."""
        ...


@lru_cache(maxsize=8)
def _resolve(names: tuple[str, ...]) -> tuple[PhaseHook, ...]:
    return tuple(HOOKS.create(name) for name in names)


def resolve_hooks(run_cfg: RunConfig) -> tuple[PhaseHook, ...]:
    """The run's configured hook chain (resolved once per distinct chain)."""
    names = DEFAULT_HOOKS if run_cfg.hooks is None else tuple(run_cfg.hooks)
    return _resolve(tuple(names))


def run_hook_chain(
    phase: str, chain, run_cfg: RunConfig | None = None, **ctx
) -> None:
    """Execute ``phase`` on every hook in ``chain`` that defines it, in order.

    A hook's ``AqaError`` propagates (validator verdict); any other exception
    is logged at WARNING and skipped.
    """
    for hook in chain or ():
        fn = getattr(hook, phase, None)
        if fn is None:
            continue
        _log.debug("hook %s.%s", getattr(hook, "name", hook), phase)
        try:
            fn(run_cfg, **ctx)
        except AqaError:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - hooks never crash a run
            _log.warning("hook %s.%s failed (ignored): %s",
                         getattr(hook, "name", hook), phase, exc)


def run_hooks(phase: str, run_cfg: RunConfig, **ctx) -> None:
    """Resolve the run's chain and execute ``phase`` on it (see run_hook_chain)."""
    run_hook_chain(phase, resolve_hooks(run_cfg), run_cfg, **ctx)

{"content": """"Phase-hook layer tests: protocol/registration, config, seed hooks, wiring."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pytest
from safetensors.numpy import save_file

import aqa.pipeline as P
from aqa.agent.fix_loop import FixResult
from aqa.config import parse_run_config
from aqa.eval.registry import BenchmarkResult, EvalResult
from aqa.hooks import (
    DEFAULT_HOOKS,
    PhaseHook,
    resolve_hooks,
    run_hook_chain,
    run_hooks,
)
from aqa.hooks.sanity import EvalSanityHook, QuantSanityHook
from aqa.logging_util import AqaError, ConfigError
from aqa.quantize import run_quantization
from aqa.registry import _BUILTINS, HOOKS

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


# ── registration: builtins + entry-point dual track ──────────────────────────
def test_hooks_registered_in_builtins_and_pyproject():
    assert _BUILTINS["aqa.hooks"] == {
        "quant_sanity": "aqa.hooks.sanity:QuantSanityHook",
        "eval_sanity": "aqa.hooks.sanity:EvalSanityHook",
    }
    assert set(HOOKS.names()) >= {"quant_sanity", "eval_sanity"}
    assert HOOKS.create("quant_sanity").name == "quant_sanity"
    assert HOOKS.create("eval_sanity").name == "eval_sanity"
    # entry-point group mirrors the builtins (installed installs expose them)
    pyproject = (REPO_ROOT / "pyproject.toml").read_text()
    assert '[project.entry-points."aqa.hooks"]' in pyproject
    assert 'quant_sanity = "aqa.hooks.sanity:QuantSanityHook"' in pyproject
    assert 'eval_sanity = "aqa.hooks.sanity:EvalSanityHook"' in pyproject


def test_runtime_registration_dual_track():
    HOOKS.register("tmp_hook", "aqa.hooks.sanity:EvalSanityHook")
    try:
        assert "tmp_hook" in HOOKS.names()
        assert isinstance(HOOKS.create("tmp_hook"), EvalSanityHook)
    finally:
        HOOKS._extra.pop("tmp_hook", None)


def test_protocol_conformance():
    class _Full:
        name = "full"

        def after_quantize(self, run_cfg, quant_cfg, output_dir):
            ...

        def after_benchmark(self, run_cfg, recipe, result_or_exception, out_dir):
            ...

    assert isinstance(_Full(), PhaseHook)
    # hooks may implement only the phases they care about
    assert not isinstance(EvalSanityHook(), PhaseHook)


# ── config ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def test_hooks_config_default_explicit_empty():
    assert parse_run_config({"model": "org/m"}).hooks is None
    assert [h.name for h in resolve_hooks(parse_run_config({"model": "org/m"}))] \
        == list(DEFAULT_HOOKS)
    cfg = parse_run_config({"model": "org/m", "hooks": ["eval_sanity"]})
    assert [h.name for h in resolve_hooks(cfg)] == ["eval_sanity"]
    assert resolve_hooks(parse_run_config({"model": "org/m", "hooks": []})) == ()


def test_hooks_config_unknown_name_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="unknown hook"):
        parse_run_config({"model": "org/m", "hooks": ["nope"]})


# ── quant_sanity ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def _write_st(dirpath: Path, keys: list[str]) -> None:
    dirpath.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tensors = {k: np.zeros((2, 2), dtype=np.float32) for k in keys}
    save_file(tensors, str(dirpath / "model.safetensors"))


def _claim_autoround(dirpath: Path, quant_method="auto-round") -> None:
    dirpath.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cfg = json.loads((dirpath / "config.json").read_text()) \
        if (dirpath / "config.json").exists() else {}
    cfg["quantization_config"] = {"quant_method": quant_method, "bits": 4}
    (dirpath / "config.json").write_text(json.dumps(cfg))


def test_quant_sanity_fails_on_claimed_but_unpacked_export(tmp_path):
    out = tmp_path / "quant"
    _claim_autoround(out)
    _write_st(out, ["model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight"])  # plain weights only
    with pytest.raises(AqaError, match="0 packed layers"):
        QuantSanityHook().after_quantize(None, None, out)


def test_quant_sanity_passes_with_packed_weights(tmp_path):
    out = tmp_path / "quant"
    _claim_autoround(out)
    _write_st(out, ["model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.qweight"])
    QuantSanityHook().after_quantize(None, None, out)  # no raise


def test_quant_sanity_passes_without_quantization_config(tmp_path):
    out = tmp_path / "quant"
    _write_st(out, ["model.layers.0.weight"])  # config.json is "{}"
    QuantSanityHook().after_quantize(None, None, out)
    (out / "config.json").unlink()
    QuantSanityHook().after_quantize(None, None, out)  # no config at all


def test_quant_sanity_diffusion_component_layout(tmp_path):
    out = tmp_path / "quant"
    _claim_autoround(out / "transformer")
    _write_st(out / "transformer", ["blocks.0.attn.to_q.weight"])  # unpacked!
    _write_st(out / "text_encoder", ["model.layers.0.mlp.weight"])
    with pytest.raises(AqaError, match="0 packed layers"):
        QuantSanityHook().after_quantize(None, None, out)
    _write_st(out / "transformer", ["blocks.0.attn.to_q.qweight"])
    QuantSanityHook().after_quantize(None, None, out)


def test_quant_sanity_auto_round_format_claims_via_quant_cfg(tmp_path):
    from aqa.config import QuantConfig

    out = tmp_path / "quant"
    out.mkdir()
    # quantization_config without an explicit auto-round quant_method
    (out / "config.json").write_text(json.dumps({"quantization_config": {"bits": 4}}))
    _write_st(out, ["model.layers.0.weight"])
    cfg = QuantConfig(export_format="auto_round")
    with pytest.raises(AqaError, match="0 packed layers"):
        QuantSanityHook().after_quantize(None, cfg, out)
    # a different format does not claim auto-round -> passes
    QuantSanityHook().after_quantize(None, QuantConfig(export_format="llm_compressor"), out)


# ── eval_sanity ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def test_eval_sanity_zero_score_fails_normal_passes(tmp_path):
    hook = EvalSanityHook()
    zero = BenchmarkResult(name="piqa", score=0.0, metric="acc")
    with pytest.raises(AqaError, match="piqa.*acc=0"):
        hook.after_benchmark(None, None, zero, tmp_path)
    ok = BenchmarkResult(name="piqa", score=0.5, metric="acc")
    hook.after_benchmark(None, None, ok, tmp_path)
    # harness failures are surfaced by the runner, not re-failed by the hook
    hook.after_benchmark(None, None, RuntimeError("boom"), tmp_path)


# ── runner semantics ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def test_hook_crash_is_logged_not_fatal():
    calls = []

    class _Crash:
        name = "crash"

        def after_benchmark(self, run_cfg, **ctx):
            raise RuntimeError("kaput")

    class _Good:
        name = "good"

        def after_benchmark(self, run_cfg, **ctx):
            calls.append("good")

    run_hook_chain("after_benchmark", [_Crash(), _Good()], None)
    assert calls == ["good"]  # the crash did not stop the chain


def test_hook_ordering_and_validator_propagation():
    calls = []

    class _Rec:
        def __init__(self, name):
            self.name = name

        def after_quantize(self, run_cfg, **ctx):
            calls.append(self.name)

    class _Veto:
        name = "veto"

        def after_quantize(self, run_cfg, **ctx):
            raise AqaError("vetoed")

    run_hook_chain("after_quantize", [_Rec("a"), _Rec("b")], None)
    assert calls == ["a", "b"]
    with pytest.raises(AqaError, match="vetoed"):
        run_hook_chain("after_quantize", [_Veto(), _Rec("c")], None)
    assert calls == ["a", "b"]  # the validator aborted the chain


def test_run_hooks_respects_config(tmp_path):
    cfg = parse_run_config({"model": "org/m", "hooks": []})
    out = tmp_path / "quant"
    _claim_autoround(out)
    _write_st(out, ["model.layers.0.weight"])
    run_hooks("after_quantize", cfg, quant_cfg=None, output_dir=out)  # all off: no raise
    cfg = parse_run_config({"model": "org/m"})  # defaults on
    with pytest.raises(AqaError, match="0 packed layers"):
        run_hooks("after_quantize", cfg, quant_cfg=None, output_dir=out)

def test_run_quantization_invokes_after_quantize_hooks(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    out = tmp_path / "quant"

    def _fake_autoround(cmd, output_dir):
        _claim_autoround(output_dir)
        _write_st(output_dir, ["model.layers.0.weight"])  # claimed but unpacked

    captured = {}

230	## Evaluation: harnesses, task grouping, and model_args
231	
232	`eval` selects a **harness** (`lm_eval` default, `native`, or `evalscope` plugin)
233	and an infra **backend** (`hf` | `vllm`). Harness-specific knobs live in per-method
234	blocks so the eval methods stay cleanly separated:
235	
236	```yaml
237	eval:
238	  benchmarks: [piqa, hellaswag, mmlu, gsm8k]
239	  backend: vllm
240	  harness: lm_eval
241	  lm_eval:
242	    model_args: { enable_thinking: false, reasoning_parser: qwen3, max_num_seqs: 128 }
243	    gen_kwargs: { max_gen_toks: 2048 }   # default --gen_kwargs for generative tasks
244	    group: true                          # merge compatible tasks into one call
245	    seed: 42
246	  evalscope: { }                         # options forwarded to the evalscope plugin
247	```
248	
249	- **`model_args`** are appended to the backend's `--model_args` (user keys override
250	  defaults) — e.g. Qwen3 reasoning models set `enable_thinking=False,reasoning_parser=qwen3`.
251	- **Task grouping** (`group: true`) runs `piqa,hellaswag,mmlu` in **one** `lm_eval`
252	  call (one model load), while `gsm8k` — which needs `--apply_chat_template
253	  --fewshot_as_multiturn` — runs **separately**. Tasks are grouped by matching
254	  generation params; incompatible tasks each get their own invocation.
255	
256	**Where per-task params live.** A benchmark's own knobs — `type` (generative vs
257	loglikelihood), `apply_chat_template`, `fewshot_as_multiturn`, `num_fewshot`,
258	`gen_kwargs`, `batch_size`, `scoring` — belong in its recipe file
259	`recipes/benchmarks/<task>.yaml` (single source of truth), **not** in every
260	`run.yaml`. For example `recipes/benchmarks/gsm8k.yaml` pins gsm8k to
261	`generative + apply_chat_template + fewshot_as_multiturn + num_fewshot:5 +
262	batch_size:"64"`, so any run that lists `gsm8k` gets the correct settings and the
263	runner automatically isolates it from the loglikelihood group. Use the `eval.*`
264	blocks only for run-wide policy (backend, global batch size, seed, model_args).
265	
266	**Breadth via lm_eval passthrough.** Any lm_eval task name works even without a
267	recipe file — `benchmarks: [<task>]` synthesises a bare `lm_eval` passthrough, so
268	lm-eval-harness's full catalogue is reachable. Curated recipes just pin the
269	*correct* per-task settings so a task "just works": shipped ones include a broad
270	instruct/base suite — `gpqa_diamond`, `mmlu_pro`, `ifeval`,
271	`bbh`, `truthfulqa`, `winogrande`, `openbookqa` (alongside `mmlu`, `gsm8k`,
272	`hellaswag`, `arc_challenge`, `piqa`). Add one file to onboard the next task; you

## Files added

- **`aqa/hooks/__init__.py`** — `PhaseHook` runtime-checkable protocol (`name` + `after_quantize(run_cfg, quant_cfg, output_dir)` / `after_benchmark(run_cfg, recipe, result_or_exception, out_dir)`; hooks implement only the phases they care about). `DEFAULT_HOOKS = ("quant_sanity", "eval_sanity")`. `resolve_hooks(run_cfg)` resolves the chain once per distinct chain via `lru_cache` on the names tuple. `run_hook_chain(phase, chain, run_cfg=None, **ctx)`: in-order execution, DEBUG log per invocation, `AqaError` propagates (validator verdict), any other exception logged at WARNING and skipped. `run_hooks(phase, run_cfg, **ctx)` = resolve + execute.
- **`aqa/hooks/sanity.py`** — the two seed validators:
  - `QuantSanityHook.after_quantize`: collects dirs claiming auto-round (`config.json` with `quantization_config.quant_method in {"auto-round","auto_round"}` at export root / `transformer/` / `unet/`, or an `export_format: auto_round` run), then header-only safetensors reads (`safe_open`, lazy import) looking for any `qweight` tensor. No claiming config → pass (fake format); any packed weights → pass; unreadable/missing safetensors lib → pass (no guessing); else `AqaError("quantization produced 0 packed layers ...")`.
  - `EvalSanityHook.after_benchmark`: `Exception` inputs pass through (runner surfaces those); a `BenchmarkResult` with `score == 0` raises `AqaError("benchmark <name> scored 0 (acc=0 => fail; ...)")`.
- **`tests/test_hooks.py`** (18 tests) — builtins/entry-point parity (pyproject text-checked), runtime `Registry.register` dual-track, protocol conformance (full impl isinstance-True; partial impl isinstance-False, documenting the skip-semantics), config default/explicit/`[]`/unknown→`ConfigError`, quant_sanity fixtures using the real `safetensors.numpy.save_file` style from `test_export_repair.py` (LLM root + diffusion component layouts, packed/unpacked/no-config/format-claim variants), eval_sanity zero/normal/exception, crash-not-fatal + chain continues, ordering, validator aborts chain, `hooks: []` vs default via `run_hooks`, `run_quantization` integration (monkeypatched `_run_autoround`), pipeline `_run_quantize` phase failure via the hook, pipeline `_run_evaluate` phase with faked `run_fix_loop`/`run_evaluation`, and the hooks-off legacy-behavior case.

The inline all-zero check is untouched.

## Deviations

1. **`eval_sanity` is per-benchmark-zero, not aggregate-all-zero.** The spec text ("raises AqaError for an all-zero benchmark result") allowed both readings; per-benchmark catches the realistic silent-breakage case in multi-benchmark runs (e.g. one misconfigured diffusion benchmark amid healthy lm ones) and feeds the fix-loop per benchmark name. The pipeline's aggregate all-zero check stays verbatim, so `hooks: []` restores exact legacy behavior; no existing pipeline test produces zero scores through the phase, so nothing needed adjusting. Note the consequence: with default hooks on, a partially-zero multi-benchmark eval now fails the phase into the fix-loop (soft-fails to the last result if unresolved — existing `_run_evaluate` semantics, covered by the test).
2. **`after_benchmark` hooks run only in the fix-loop-wrapped `_phase`**, matching where the inline check lives; the `fix_loop: false` evaluate path bypassed *all* such checks before and still does (parity, minimal diff).
3. **Quantize hook ctx passes `run_cfg=None`** from `run_quantization`/`run_quant_command` (they don't receive one); the protocol tolerates it and `quant_sanity` only needs `output_dir`/`quant_cfg`. This keeps the "thread minimal context without breaking signatures" constraint.
4. **Unverifiable ≠ failure in `quant_sanity`** (missing safetensors lib / unreadable shard / zero shards… zero shards actually *does* fail since it's verifiably packed-free; only `None` states pass) — a validator that guesses would false-positive on exotic exports.

357	    def _replay_reference(self, error_text: str, *, max_candidates: int = 2,
358	                          inline_threshold: int = 1500, total_budget: int = 3000) -> str:
359	        """Format recorded fixes for THIS failure as agent *reference* (Option A).
360	
361	        We deliberately do NOT auto-apply recorded patches: a diff captured on a
362	        different model/checkpoint can silently break the environment, and the
363	        revert path is itself risky. Instead the best-matching recorded diffs +
364	        their provenance are handed to the agent, which decides whether the
365	        mechanism applies to the current model/checkpoint and adapts or ignores it.
366	
367	        To keep the prompt lean, only SMALL diffs are inlined; a large (e.g.
368	        multi-file source) patch is summarised (files touched, +/- line counts)
369	        with a pointer to its on-disk path for the agent to read on demand -- never
370	        hard-truncated mid-hunk. A running ``total_budget`` caps inlined bytes so
371	        two large candidates cannot both bloat the prompt. Returns "" when replay
372	        is disabled, there is no knowledge store, or nothing matches.
373	        """
374	        if not (self.replay and self.knowledge):
375	            return ""
376	        try:
377	            records = self.knowledge.find_patches(self.phase_name, error_text)
378	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - lookup is best-effort
379	            _log.warning("replay: lookup failed: %s", exc)
380	            return ""
381	        blocks: list[str] = []
382	        remaining = total_budget
383	        for rec in records[:max_candidates]:
384	            prov = (f"model={rec.model_id or '?'} scheme={rec.scheme or '?'} "
385	                    f"class={rec.error_class or '?'} sig={rec.sig_hash}")
386	            diff = rec.diff_text(max_chars=inline_threshold + 1)
387	            if diff and len(diff) <= inline_threshold and len(diff) <= remaining:
388	                remaining -= len(diff)
389	                blocks.append(f"### candidate ({prov})\n```diff\n{diff}\n```")
390	            else:
391	                # Too big to inline: summarise + point the agent at the patch on disk.
392	                paths = ", ".join(rec.patch_paths())
393	                blocks.append(
394	                    f"### candidate ({prov})\n{rec.stat_summary()}\n"
395	                    f"full patch on disk (READ it if the mechanism looks relevant): {paths}")
396	        if not blocks:
397	            return ""
398	        _log.info("replay: injecting %d recorded fix(es) as reference for %s "
399	                  "(no auto-apply)", len(blocks), self.phase_name)
400	        return "\n\n".join(blocks)
