1	"""Build the structured fix-attempt prompt for the agent.
2	
3	Ports ``build_fix_prompt`` from ``local_dispatch/agent/agent_fix_loop.sh``.  The
4	prompt asks the agent to emit a strict, machine-parseable analysis block first
5	(COMPONENT / ERROR_CLASS / ... / VERDICT / SMOKE_TEST) -- this is what
6	:mod:`aqa.agent.verdict` parses to drive the escalation/drift state machine.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	_FIX_PLAYBOOK_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "recipes" / "fix_playbook.md"
14	
15	
16	def load_fix_playbook() -> str:
17	    """Return the packaged fix-agent troubleshooting playbook (best-effort).
18	
19	    This is durable, cross-run domain knowledge embedded into every fix prompt as
20	    REFERENCE. A missing/unreadable asset degrades gracefully to an empty string.
21	    Per-run, box/model-specific guidance should go through ``agent.context`` instead.
22	    """
23	    try:
24	        return _FIX_PLAYBOOK_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
25	    except OSError:
26	        return ""
27	
28	
29	_PROTOCOL = """\
30	You MUST print the block below FIRST, before changing any code or installing anything.
31	Do NOT modify code until you have printed an EVIDENCE_RESULT from a READ-ONLY command
32	that supports your hypothesis. No guessing.
33	
34	COMPONENT: <our_code|transformers|auto_round|vllm|vllm_omni|diffusers|torch|model_code|data|environment>
35	ERROR_CLASS: <ONE stable snake_case token naming THIS error's category. Reuse the same
36	             token every time the same underlying error recurs (drives drift detection).>
37	ROOT_CAUSE_HYPOTHESIS: <one falsifiable sentence -- the specific cause>
38	EVIDENCE_CMD: <a single read-only command that verifies the hypothesis>
39	EVIDENCE_RESULT: <paste the command's output>
40	VERDICT: <FIXABLE | UNFIXABLE | ESCALATE>
41	UNFIXABLE_REASON: <required only if UNFIXABLE>
42	FIX_TIER: <config | upgrade | workaround | patch>   # always try the LOWEST that works
43	FIX_PLAN: <3 lines max -- what you will change and why it fixes the ROOT CAUSE>
44	SMOKE_TEST: <ONE fast, MECHANISM-LEVEL command that proves the FIX MECHANISM holds.
45	             Target ~30s. It must NOT be the full phase: do NOT run full lm_eval, do NOT
46	             boot the whole vLLM engine / load the whole model, do NOT re-quantize end to
47	             end -- the harness re-runs the FULL phase itself to verify, so duplicating it
48	             only burns your time budget. Instead verify the SPECIFIC thing your fix
49	             changed, e.g.: `python -c "import <edited_module>"` or `python -m py_compile
50	             <edited_file>` (edit didn't break imports/syntax); read the checkpoint's
51	             quantization config JSON and assert the offending layer is now in the
52	             ignore-list; read a safetensors HEADER (not a full load) and assert an edited
53	             weight's dtype; or import JUST the failing kernel/layer and call it once on a
54	             tiny dummy tensor of the offending shape to reproduce (or clear) the exact
55	             assertion. Prefer the cheapest check that exercises the SAME mechanism the
56	             error came from.>
57	
58	## Rules
59	- If VERDICT is UNFIXABLE: print the block and STOP (no wasted retries).
60	- If the fix needs a MORE CAPABLE model (deep multi-file reasoning, subtle mixed-precision
61	  layout, hard custom-model patch), set VERDICT: ESCALATE and STOP with a clear reason.
62	- Prefer the LOWEST FIX_TIER; patching source is a last resort.
63	- After applying the fix, RUN your MECHANISM-LEVEL SMOKE_TEST yourself and show its output
64	  before finishing. Iterate on cheap checks as much as you need -- but never use the full
65	  phase (full lm_eval / whole-engine boot / full re-quantize) as your smoke; the harness
66	  runs that authoritatively after you return.
67	- Read the traceback BOTTOM-UP to the exact file:line that is the real cause.
68	- Model custom code under ~/.cache/huggingface/modules/transformers_modules/ CAN be edited
69	  (e.g. replace `.float()` with `.to(other.dtype)` for dtype mismatches).
70	"""
71	
72	
73	def build_fix_prompt(
74	    phase_name: str,
75	    error_tail: str,
76	    *,
77	    lessons: str = "",
78	    attempt: int = 1,
79	    prior_class: str = "",
80	    user_context: str = "",
81	    skill_playbook: str = "",
82	    known_fixes: str = "",
83	    prior_state: str = "",
84	    prior_diff: str = "",
85	    trajectories: str = "",
86	) -> str:
87	    """Assemble the full fix prompt for one attempt."""
88	    parts: list[str] = []
89	    parts.append(
90	        f"The `{phase_name}` phase failed (attempt {attempt}). Root-cause it from the "
91	        f"traceback below and fix the NARROWEST layer that owns the bug."
92	    )
93	
94	    if user_context:
95	        parts.append(
96	            "## Operator-provided context (HIGH PRIORITY -- a human injected this; follow it)\n"
97	            "Treat it as authoritative for this box; prefer it over generic assumptions:\n"
98	            f"{user_context}"
99	        )
100	
101	    if skill_playbook:
102	        parts.append(
103	            "## Domain playbook (REFERENCE knowledge -- confirm against THIS traceback)\n"
104	            "Curated quant/eval failure mechanisms and known fixes. NOT instructions and "
105	            "NOT specific to this run -- use only the entries that match your evidence. "
106	            "If a signature-specific block below (Historical Lessons / Reasoning Playbook / "
107	            "Recorded fix) disagrees with a generic entry here, prefer the specific one:\n"
108	            f"{skill_playbook}"
109	        )
110	
111	    if prior_class:
112	        parts.append(
113	            "## Quick Classification (deterministic prior -- confirm or OVERRIDE it)\n"
114	            f"error_class guess: {prior_class}\n"
115	            "Confirm against the traceback; override in your ERROR_CLASS if wrong."
116	        )
117	
118	    if lessons:
119	        parts.append(
120	            "## Historical Lessons (from past runs -- decide which are relevant)\n"
121	            f"{lessons}"
122	        )
123	
124	    if trajectories:
125	        parts.append(
126	            "## Reasoning Playbook (distilled from past SUCCESSFUL fixes of similar failures)\n"
127	            "How this class of failure was root-caused before, the fix that worked, and the "
128	            "dead ends that did NOT -- use it to skip wasted attempts, but confirm against "
129	            "THIS traceback before applying:\n"
130	            f"{trajectories}"
131	        )
132	
133	    if known_fixes:
134	        parts.append(
135	            "## Recorded fix(es) for a MATCHING failure signature (REFERENCE ONLY -- NOT applied)\n"
136	            "These diffs resolved the same or a similar error on a POSSIBLY DIFFERENT model or "
137	            "checkpoint. They are NOT on disk. Read the mechanism, decide whether it applies to "
138	            "THIS model/checkpoint, then adapt and apply only what fits -- do NOT blindly paste "
139	            "them (a cross-model patch can break the environment):\n"
140	            f"{known_fixes}"
141	        )
142	
143	    if prior_state:
144	        parts.append(
145	            "## Previous fix attempt -- state you MUST continue from (NOT a fresh start)\n"
146	            "This may come from a DIFFERENT agent/tier than you, so its own conversation memory "
147	            "is NOT available to you -- rely on this block. The 'ACTUAL re-run' line is the "
148	            "harness's own authoritative verdict (the agent's self-report can be wrong or "
149	            "missing):\n"
150	            f"{prior_state}"
151	        )
152	
153	    if prior_diff:
154	        parts.append(
155	            "## Changes ALREADY made by earlier fix tiers (consolidate, don't restart)\n"
156	            "You are the STRONGEST tier and the patch CONSOLIDATOR. This unified diff is on "
157	            "disk now; keep what helps, fix what is wrong or incomplete:\n"
158	            f"```diff\n{prior_diff}\n```"
159	        )
160	
161	    parts.append(f"## Error output (tail)\n```\n{error_tail}\n```")
162	    parts.append(_PROTOCOL)
163	    return "\n\n".join(parts)

1	"""Parse structured fields and the verdict from an agent's fix-attempt output.
2	
3	Ports the ``agent_verdict`` / ``extract_agent_field`` logic from
4	``local_dispatch/agent/agent_fix_loop.sh``.  The parsing is deliberately strict:
5	only a line whose ``VERDICT:`` value is exactly one of the tokens counts, so prose
6	like *"Only declare VERDICT: UNFIXABLE for ..."* or the placeholder
7	``VERDICT: <FIXABLE | ...>`` is ignored.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import re
13	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
14	from enum import Enum
15	
16	
17	class Verdict(str, Enum):
18	    FIXABLE = "fixable"
19	    UNFIXABLE = "unfixable"
20	    ESCALATE = "escalate"
21	
22	
23	# A real verdict line: optional markdown/bullets, VERDICT:, EXACTLY one token, EOL.
24	_VERDICT_RE = re.compile(
25	    r"^[\s>*\-]*VERDICT\s*:?\s*\**\s*(FIXABLE|UNFIXABLE|ESCALATE)\s*\.?\**\s*$",
26	    re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE,
27	)
28	
29	# The single-line labels the protocol asks the agent to emit.
30	_LABELS = (
31	    "COMPONENT",
32	    "ERROR_CLASS",
33	    "ROOT_CAUSE_HYPOTHESIS",
34	    "EVIDENCE_CMD",
35	    "EVIDENCE_RESULT",
36	    "VERDICT",
37	    "UNFIXABLE_REASON",
38	    "FIX_TIER",
39	    "FIX_PLAN",
40	    "SMOKE_TEST",
41	)
42	
43	
44	def parse_verdict(text: str) -> Verdict | None:
45	    """Return the LAST valid verdict in ``text`` (later attempts override), or None.
46	
47	    Placeholder lines (``VERDICT: <FIXABLE | UNFIXABLE | ESCALATE>``) never match
48	    because the captured group would have to be a single bare token.
49	    """
50	    matches = _VERDICT_RE.findall(text or "")
51	    if not matches:
52	        return None
53	    return Verdict(matches[-1].lower())
54	
55	
56	def extract_field(text: str, label: str, max_len: int = 200) -> str:
57	    """Pull a labeled single-line field's value (last occurrence wins)."""
58	    if not text:
59	        return ""
60	    pat = re.compile(
61	        rf"^[\s>*\-]*{re.escape(label)}\s*:?\s*\**\s*(.+?)\s*\**\s*$",
62	        re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE,
63	    )
64	    values = [m.group(1).strip() for m in pat.finditer(text)]
65	    # Drop placeholder values like "<ONE stable snake_case token ...>".
66	    values = [v for v in values if not (v.startswith("<") and v.endswith(">"))]
67	    if not values:
68	        return ""
69	    return values[-1][:max_len]
70	
71	
72	def _normalize_class(raw: str) -> str:
73	    """Normalize an ERROR_CLASS token to a stable snake_case identifier."""
74	    tok = raw.strip().split()[0] if raw.strip() else ""
75	    tok = tok.lower()
76	    tok = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_]", "", tok)
77	    return tok
78	
79	
80	@dataclass
81	class AgentAnalysis:
82	    """Structured view of one agent fix attempt's output."""
83	
84	    verdict: Verdict | None = None
85	    component: str = ""
86	    error_class: str = ""
87	    root_cause: str = ""
88	    unfixable_reason: str = ""
89	    fix_tier: str = ""
90	    fix_plan: str = ""
91	    smoke_test: str = ""
92	    raw: str = field(default="", repr=False)
93	
94	    @classmethod
95	    def parse(cls, text: str) -> AgentAnalysis:
96	        return cls(
97	            verdict=parse_verdict(text),
98	            component=extract_field(text, "COMPONENT", 60),
99	            error_class=_normalize_class(extract_field(text, "ERROR_CLASS", 60)),
100	            root_cause=extract_field(text, "ROOT_CAUSE_HYPOTHESIS", 400),
101	            unfixable_reason=extract_field(text, "UNFIXABLE_REASON", 200),
102	            fix_tier=extract_field(text, "FIX_TIER", 40),
103	            fix_plan=extract_field(text, "FIX_PLAN", 400),
104	            smoke_test=extract_field(text, "SMOKE_TEST", 400),
105	            raw=text or "",
106	        )
107	
108	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
109	        d = {
110	            "verdict": self.verdict.value if self.verdict else None,
111	            "component": self.component,
112	            "error_class": self.error_class,
113	            "root_cause": self.root_cause,
114	            "unfixable_reason": self.unfixable_reason,
115	            "fix_tier": self.fix_tier,
116	            "fix_plan": self.fix_plan,
117	            "smoke_test": self.smoke_test,
118	        }
119	        return {k: v for k, v in d.items() if v}

    def _format_history(self, history: list[dict], rejected_trail: list[str],
                        cur_class: str) -> str:
        """Render the in-run attempt history: table + error evolution + dead ends.

        Unlike ``_format_prior_state`` (only the immediately preceding attempt),
        this covers EVERY attempt of the run, so a later tier can see the whole
        path -- including which hypotheses were already ruled out (the rejected
        trail is otherwise only persisted to the trajectory store on success).
        """
        if not history:
            return ""
        lines = [
            "| # | tier | error before | progress | agent verdict | summary |",
            "|---|------|--------------|----------|---------------|---------|",
        ]
        for h in history[-6:]:  # keep the block bounded
            lines.append(
                f"| {h['attempt']} | {h['tier']} | {h['error_class'] or '?'} "
                f"| {h['progress']} | {h['verdict'] or '-'} | {h['summary'] or '-'} |"
            )
        seq = " → ".join([h["error_class"] or "?" for h in history] + [cur_class or "?"])
        evolution = f"error evolution: {seq}"
        depths = [h["progress"] for h in history]
        if any(d > 0 for d in depths):
            advanced = depths[-1] > depths[0]
            evolution += (f" -- quantize progress depth {depths[0]} → {depths[-1]} "
                          f"({'advanced' if advanced else 'NOT advanced'})")
        lines.append(evolution)
        if rejected_trail:
            lines.append("hypotheses already ruled out this run (do NOT retry these):")
            lines.extend(f"- {t}" for t in rejected_trail[-6:])
        return "\n".join(lines)", "old_string": "        files = self._prior_attempt_files(prior.attempt)

# ── inter-attempt information flow (history / evidence / evolution) ─────────


def test_agent_analysis_parses_evidence_fields():
    text = (
        "COMPONENT: vllm\n"
        "ERROR_CLASS: import_error\n"
        "EVIDENCE_CMD: python -c 'import vllm'\n"
        "EVIDENCE_RESULT: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vllm'\n"
        "VERDICT: FIXABLE\n"
    )
    a = AgentAnalysis.parse(text)
    assert a.evidence_cmd == "python -c 'import vllm'"
    assert "ModuleNotFoundError" in a.evidence_result
    assert a.to_dict()["evidence_cmd"] == "python -c 'import vllm'"
    # absent evidence -> empty fields, absent from to_dict
    b = AgentAnalysis.parse("VERDICT: FIXABLE\n")
    assert b.evidence_cmd == "" and "evidence_cmd" not in b.to_dict()


def test_build_fix_prompt_history_block_placement():
    p = build_fix_prompt("quantize", "boom", attempt=2,
                         history="TABLE", prior_state="PRIOR")

    assert p.index("Attempt history THIS run") < p.index("Previous fix attempt")
    # omitted by default (attempt-1 prompts unchanged)
    assert "Attempt history" not in build_fix_prompt("quantize", "boom")
    # the protocol tells the agent to consult the history block

# ── upgraded deterministic classification prior ──────────────────────────────

from aqa.agent.drift import classify_error_detail  # noqa: E402
from aqa.agent.prompt import playbook_section_for  # noqa: E402


def test_classify_error_real_run_regressions():
    """Tonight's seven real GPU-run failures, pinned to their expected classes."""
    cases = [
        ("auto-round is not installed; `pip install auto-round`", "missing_tool"),
        ("Error: Access denied. This repository requires approval.", "auth_error"),
        ("RuntimeError: model parallel state must be empty before initialization; "
         "found dp, cfg, sp", "engine_reinit"),
        ("KeyError: 'layers.29.adaLN_modulation.0.qweight'", "quant_artifact"),
        ("ValueError: There is no module or parameter named "
         "'text_encoder.embed_tokens' in ZImagePipeline...", "quant_artifact"),
        ("ValueError: Sequence length must be less than max_position_embeddings "
         "(got 127 and 77)", "context_length"),
        ("PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root/x'", "permission_error"),
    ]
    for text, expected in cases:
        assert classify_error(text) == expected, text


def test_classify_error_rule_ordering_guards():
    # missing_tool fires before import_error even inside an ImportError message
    assert classify_error("ImportError: auto-round is not installed") == "missing_tool"
    # quant_artifact fires before the coarse exception buckets
    assert classify_error("KeyError: 'model.layers.0.qweight'") == "quant_artifact"
    # engine_reinit fires before vllm_engine_error / runtime_error buckets
    assert classify_error("RuntimeError: model parallel state must be empty") \
        == "engine_reinit"
    # context_length fires before the value_error bucket
    assert classify_error("ValueError: Sequence length must be less than "
                          "max_position_embeddings") == "context_length"
    # checkpoint_key_mismatch keeps its own patterns even when a packed-weight
    # name appears in the same line
    assert classify_error("RuntimeError: Missing key(s) in state_dict: 'layers.0.qweight'") \
        == "checkpoint_key_mismatch"


def test_classify_error_wrapper_compatibility():
    # the wrapper stays a thin alias returning exactly the detail's class name
    for text in ("torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory",
                 "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'auto_round'",
                 "something totally unknown here"):
        assert classify_error(text) == classify_error_detail(text).class_name


def test_classify_error_detail_fields():
    d = classify_error_detail("line one\ntorch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory")
    assert d.class_name == "oom"
    assert d.rule_id.startswith("oom#")
    assert d.evidence == "torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory"
    assert len(d.evidence) <= 200
    long_line = "CUDA out of memory " + "y" * 500
    assert len(classify_error_detail(long_line).evidence) <= 200
    unknown = classify_error_detail("totally opaque")
    assert unknown.class_name == "unknown"
    assert unknown.rule_id == "" and unknown.evidence == ""


def test_classification_prompt_block_with_evidence():
    p = build_fix_prompt("quantize", "boom", prior_class="oom",
                         prior_evidence="torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory")
    assert "error_class guess: oom (matched: torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError" in p
    # no evidence -> the block keeps its exact previous format
    p2 = build_fix_prompt("quantize", "boom", prior_class="oom")
    assert "error_class guess: oom\n" in p2


def test_playbook_section_pointer():
    assert playbook_section_for("oom") == "OOM / memory"
    assert playbook_section_for("quant_artifact") == "Diffusion (vllm-omni text-to-image)"
    assert playbook_section_for("engine_reinit") == "Diffusion (vllm-omni text-to-image)"
    assert playbook_section_for("unmapped_class") == ""
    p = build_fix_prompt("quantize", "boom", skill_playbook="BODY",
                         playbook_pointer="OOM / memory")
    assert "The section most relevant to this class: OOM / memory" in p
    assert p.index("most relevant to this class") < p.index("BODY")  # pointer before content
    p2 = build_fix_prompt("quantize", "boom", skill_playbook="BODY")
    assert "most relevant to this class" not in p2


def test_fix_loop_prompt_shows_evidence_and_pointer(tmp_path: Path):
    results = [PhaseResult(ok=False, log_text="torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA OOM"),
               PhaseResult(ok=True)]
    runner = _recording_runner(["VERDICT: FIXABLE\nFIX_PLAN: lower mem"])
    loop = FixLoop(
        "quantize", lambda: results.pop(0),
        config=FixLoopConfig(tiers=["openclaw", "opus"]),
        out_dir=tmp_path, run_agent=runner,
    )
    assert loop.run().ok
    p1 = runner.prompts[0]
    assert "error_class guess: oom (matched: torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError" in p1
    assert "The section most relevant to this class: OOM / memory" in p1

import argparse
import os
import os.path as osp
import time
from collections import defaultdict

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
from accelerate import Accelerator
from accelerate.utils import gather_object
from PIL import Image
from tqdm import tqdm


def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="DPG-Bench evaluation.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--image-root-path",
        type=str,
        default=None,
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--resolution",
        type=int,
        default=None,
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--csv",
        type=str,
        default='./dpg_bench/dpg_bench.csv',
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--res-path",
        type=str,
        default=None,
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--pic-num",
        type=int,
        default=1,
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--vqa-model",
        type=str,
        default='mplug',
    )

    args = parser.parse_args()
    return args


class MPLUG(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, ckpt='damo/mplug_visual-question-answering_coco_large_en', device='gpu'):
        super().__init__()
        from modelscope.pipelines import pipeline
        from modelscope.utils.constant import Tasks
        self.pipeline_vqa = pipeline(Tasks.visual_question_answering, model=ckpt, device=device)

    def vqa(self, image, question):
        input_vqa = {'image': image, 'question': question}
        result = self.pipeline_vqa(input_vqa)
        return result['text']

def prepare_dpg_data(args):
    previous_id = ''
    current_id = ''
    question_dict = dict()
    category_count = defaultdict(int)
    # 'item_id', 'text', 'keywords', 'proposition_id', 'dependency', 'category_broad', 'category_detailed', 'tuple', 'question_natural_language'
    data = pd.read_csv(args.csv)
    for i, line in data.iterrows():
        if i == 0:
            continue

        current_id = line.item_id
        qid = int(line.proposition_id)
        dependency_list_str = line.dependency.split(',')
        dependency_list_int = []
        for d in dependency_list_str:
            d_int = int(d.strip())
            dependency_list_int.append(d_int)

        if current_id == previous_id:
            question_dict[current_id]['qid2tuple'][qid] = line.tuple
            question_dict[current_id]['qid2dependency'][qid] = dependency_list_int
            question_dict[current_id]['qid2question'][qid] = line.question_natural_language
        else:
            question_dict[current_id] = dict(
                qid2tuple={qid: line.tuple},
                qid2dependency={qid: dependency_list_int},
                qid2question={qid: line.question_natural_language})
        
        category = line.question_natural_language.split('(')[0].strip()
        category_count[category] += 1
        
        previous_id = current_id

    return question_dict

def crop_image(input_image, crop_tuple=None):
    if crop_tuple is None:
        return input_image

    cropped_image = input_image.crop((crop_tuple[0], crop_tuple[1], crop_tuple[2], crop_tuple[3]))

    return cropped_image

def compute_dpg_one_sample(args, question_dict, image_path, vqa_model, resolution):
    generated_image = Image.open(image_path)
    crop_tuples_list = [
        (0,0,resolution,resolution),
        (resolution, 0, resolution*2, resolution),
        (0, resolution, resolution, resolution*2),
        (resolution, resolution, resolution*2, resolution*2),
    ]

    crop_tuples = crop_tuples_list[:args.pic_num]
    key = osp.basename(image_path).split('.')[0]
    value = question_dict.get(key, None)
    qid2tuple = value['qid2tuple']
    qid2question = value['qid2question']
    qid2dependency = value['qid2dependency']

    qid2answer = dict()
    qid2scores = dict()
    qid2validity = dict()

    scores = []
    for crop_tuple in crop_tuples:
        cropped_image = crop_image(generated_image, crop_tuple)
        for id, question in qid2question.items():
            answer = vqa_model.vqa(cropped_image, question)
            qid2answer[id] = answer
            qid2scores[id] = float(answer == 'yes')
            with open(args.res_path.replace('.txt', '_detail.txt'), 'a') as f:
                f.write(image_path + ', ' + str(crop_tuple) + ', ' + question + ', ' + answer + '\n')
        qid2scores_orig = qid2scores.copy()

        for id, parent_ids in qid2dependency.items():
            # zero-out scores if parent questions are answered 'no'
            any_parent_answered_no = False
            for parent_id in parent_ids:
                if parent_id == 0:
                    continue
                if qid2scores[parent_id] == 0:
                    any_parent_answered_no = True
                    break
            if any_parent_answered_no:
                qid2scores[id] = 0
                qid2validity[id] = False
            else:
                qid2validity[id] = True

        score = sum(qid2scores.values()) / len(qid2scores)
        scores.append(score)
    average_score = sum(scores) / len(scores)
    with open(args.res_path, 'a') as f:
        f.write(image_path + ', ' + ', '.join(str(i) for i in scores) + ', ' + str(average_score) + '\n')
  
    return average_score, qid2tuple, qid2scores_orig


def main():
    args = parse_args()

    accelerator = Accelerator()

    question_dict = prepare_dpg_data(args)

    timestamp = time.time()
    time_array = time.localtime(timestamp)
    time_style = time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S", time_array)
    if args.res_path is None:
        args.res_path = osp.join(args.image_root_path, f'dpg-bench_{time_style}_results.txt')

{"content": """"DPG-Bench scorer: dense-prompt-following judged by mPLUG VQA.

Port of TencentQQGYLab/ELLA's ``dpg_bench/compute_dpg_bench.py`` (Apache-2.0 --
see NOTICE; data vendored under ``recipes/data/dpgbench/``).  Per image, each
proposition question is answered by VQA (``yes``/``no``); a question's score is
zeroed when any parent proposition (dependency) scored 0.  Aggregation follows
upstream exactly, including its quirks:

* the headline DPG score is the mean over images of the per-image
  DEPENDENCY-ADJUSTED mean question score;
* the per-category breakdown instead aggregates the RAW (pre-dependency)
  per-question scores (upstream returns ``qid2scores_orig`` for categories);
* the first CSV data row is skipped in data prep (upstream
  ``if i == 0: continue``), which leaves dangling dependencies on the first
  item -- upstream's per-image ``try/except`` then skips that image, and so
  does :meth:`DpgBenchScorer.evaluate_rows`.

Heavy deps (PIL / torch / modelscope) import lazily so the module is importable
without a GPU stack; the VQA judge is only constructed when scoring runs.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Protocol

from ..logging_util import AqaError, get_logger

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover
    from collections.abc import Iterable

_log = get_logger("eval.dpgbench")

DEFAULT_VQA_MODEL = "damo/mplug_visual-question-answering_coco_large_en"
DEFAULT_RESOLUTION = 1024  # matches the harness's default generation size

DATA_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "recipes" / "data" / "dpgbench"


# ── data prep: CSV -> prompts.jsonl ──────────────────────────────────────────
def convert_dpg_csv(csv_path: str | Path, out_path: str | Path) -> list[dict]:
    """Convert the official ``dpg_bench.csv`` into one-record-per-prompt JSONL.

    Records: ``{idx, item_id, prompt, questions: [{qid, question, answer,
    dependency, category}], category}`` -- ``idx`` aligns with the diffusion
    harness's flat generation layout (``<idx>.png``).  Port of the official
    ``prepare_dpg_data`` (including its first-data-row skip, for score parity).
    """
    items: dict[str, dict] = {}
    order: list[str] = []
    with Path(csv_path).open(newline="") as fh:
        for i, row in enumerate(csv.DictReader(fh)):
            if i == 0:
                continue  # upstream quirk (kept): the first data row is dropped
            item_id = row["item_id"]
            if item_id not in items:
                items[item_id] = {"prompt": row["text"], "questions": []}
                order.append(item_id)
            items[item_id]["questions"].append({
                "qid": int(row["proposition_id"]),
                "question": row["question_natural_language"],
                "answer": row["tuple"],
                "dependency": [int(d.strip()) for d in row["dependency"].split(",")],
                # official category derivation (from the tuple column)
                "category": row["tuple"].split("(")[0].strip(),
            })
    records = []
    for idx, item_id in enumerate(order):
        questions = items[item_id]["questions"]
        records.append({
            "idx": idx,
            "item_id": item_id,
            "prompt": items[item_id]["prompt"],
            "questions": questions,
            "category": questions[0]["category"],
        })
    out_path = Path(out_path)
    out_path.write_text(
        "".join(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n" for r in records)
    )
    return records


def load_records(path: str | Path) -> list[dict]:
    """Read a converted prompts.jsonl."""
    return [json.loads(line) for line in Path(path).read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]


# ── VQA judge seam ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
class VQAJudge(Protocol):
    """Answers a yes/no question about an image (mPLUG in production, faked in tests)."""

    def vqa(self, image: Any, question: str) -> str: ...


class MPlugJudge:
    """mPLUG VQA via modelscope (``damo/mplug_visual-question-answering_*``).

    The modelscope pipeline (and its old pinned deps) is built lazily on first
    use; a construction failure surfaces as a clear :class:`AqaError`.
    """

    def __init__(self, model_id: str = DEFAULT_VQA_MODEL, device: str = "auto"):
        self.model_id = model_id
        self.device = device
        self._pipe = None

    def _build(self) -> None:
        if self._pipe is not None:
            return
        try:
            from modelscope.pipelines import pipeline
            from modelscope.utils.constant import Tasks
        except ImportError as exc:
            raise AqaError(
                "dpgbench scoring needs the modelscope mPLUG VQA stack: "
                "pip install modelscope (plus mplug's pinned deps)"
            ) from exc
        device = self.device
        if device == "auto":
            try:
                import torch
                device = "gpu" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
            except ImportError:
                device = "cpu"
        try:
            self._pipe = pipeline(
                Tasks.visual_question_answering, model=self.model_id, device=device
            )
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - old stack fails in many ways
            raise AqaError(
                f"dpgbench: failed to load VQA model {self.model_id}: {exc}"
            ) from exc

    def vqa(self, image: Any, question: str) -> str:
        self._build()
        return self._pipe({"image": image, "question": question})["text"]


# ── scoring (compute_dpg_bench.py port) ──────────────────────────────────────
def score_image(
    judge: VQAJudge,
    image: Any,
    record: dict,
    *,
    resolution: int = DEFAULT_RESOLUTION,
    pic_num: int = 1,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score one generated image against its prompt record (official logic).

    ``pic_num=1`` keeps the top-left ``resolution``-sized crop only (upstream
    default); higher values add the remaining quadrants.  Returns the per-image
    average plus both score variants (raw/pre-dependency and adjusted).
    """
    crop_tuples = [
        (0, 0, resolution, resolution),
        (resolution, 0, resolution * 2, resolution),
        (0, resolution, resolution, resolution * 2),
        (resolution, resolution, resolution * 2, resolution * 2),
    ][:pic_num]
    questions = record["questions"]
    crop_scores: list[float] = []
    raw_scores: dict[int, float] = {}
    adj_scores: dict[int, float] = {}
    answers: dict[int, str] = {}
    for crop_tuple in crop_tuples:
        cropped = image.crop(crop_tuple)
        qid2scores: dict[int, float] = {}
        for q in questions:
            answer = judge.vqa(cropped, q["question"])
            answers[q["qid"]] = answer
            qid2scores[q["qid"]] = float(answer == "yes")
        raw_scores = dict(qid2scores)  # pre-dependency (upstream: qid2scores_orig)
        # zero out a question's score when any parent proposition answered 'no'
        for q in questions:
            parents = [p for p in q["dependency"] if p != 0]
            if any(qid2scores[parent] == 0 for parent in parents):
                qid2scores[q["qid"]] = 0.0
        adj_scores = qid2scores
        crop_scores.append(sum(qid2scores.values()) / len(qid2scores))
    return {
        "score": sum(crop_scores) / len(crop_scores),
        "crop_scores": crop_scores,
        "answers": answers,
        "raw_scores": raw_scores,
        "adj_scores": adj_scores,
    }


def _question_categories(record: dict) -> dict[int, str]:
    return {q["qid"]: q["category"] for q in record["questions"]}


def summarize(image_rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Aggregate per-image rows into overall + L1/L2 category scores (official).

    Overall = mean of per-image (dependency-adjusted) scores; categories use the
    RAW per-question scores (upstream quirk, kept for parity).
    """
    overall = (sum(r["score"] for r in image_rows) / len(image_rows)) if image_rows else 0.0
    cat_scores: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
    for row in image_rows:
        for qid, cat in row["categories"].items():
            cat_scores.setdefault(cat, []).append(row["raw_scores"][qid])
    l2 = {cat: sum(v) / len(v) for cat, v in cat_scores.items()}
    l1_scores: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
    for cat, vals in cat_scores.items():
        l1_scores.setdefault(cat.split("-")[0].strip(), []).extend(vals)
    l1 = {cat: sum(v) / len(v) for cat, v in l1_scores.items()}
    return {"overall": overall, "categories": l2, "categories_l1": l1,
            "num_images": len(image_rows)}


# ── scorer (harness-facing) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
class DpgBenchScorer:
    """Evaluate a flat generated-image dir against DPG-Bench prompt records."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        vqa_model: str = DEFAULT_VQA_MODEL,
        resolution: int = DEFAULT_RESOLUTION,
        device: str = "auto",
        pic_num: int = 1,
        judge: VQAJudge | None = None,  # test seam: inject a fake judge
    ):
        self.vqa_model = vqa_model
        self.resolution = resolution
        self.device = device
        self.pic_num = pic_num
        self._judge = judge

    def judge(self) -> VQAJudge:
        """The VQA judge, constructed only when scoring actually runs."""
        if self._judge is None:
            self._judge = MPlugJudge(self.vqa_model, device=self.device)
        return self._judge

    def evaluate_rows(
        self, rows: list[dict], records: list[dict]
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Score every generated image row; returns official-diffable rows.

        ``rows`` are the harness's metadata.csv rows (idx/image_path); ``records``
        are the converted prompt records (``questions`` per prompt), aligned by
        ``idx``.  A failed image is logged and skipped (upstream try/except parity).
        """
        from PIL import Image

        judge = self.judge()
        by_idx = {int(r["idx"]): r for r in records}
        out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for row in rows:
            idx = int(row["idx"])
            record = by_idx.get(idx)
            image_path = row["image_path"]
            if record is None:
                _log.warning("dpgbench: no prompt record for idx %d; skipped", idx)
                continue
            try:
                result = score_image(
                    judge, Image.open(image_path), record,
                    resolution=self.resolution, pic_num=self.pic_num,
                )
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - upstream: 'Failed filename'
                _log.warning("dpgbench: failed to score %s: %s", image_path, exc)
                continue
            out.append({
                "filename": str(image_path),
                "idx": idx,
                "item_id": record.get("item_id", ""),
                "prompt": record["prompt"],
                "score": result["score"],
                "crop_scores": result["crop_scores"],
                "answers": {str(k): v for k, v in result["answers"].items()},
                "raw_scores": result["raw_scores"],
                "adj_scores": result["adj_scores"],
                "categories": _question_categories(record),
            })
        return out

    def write_results(self, rows: list[dict[str, Any]], out_prefix: Path) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
        """Write results.jsonl + the official-format results txt lines."""
        jsonl = out_prefix.with_suffix(".jsonl")
        jsonl.write_text("".join(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n" for r in rows))
        txt = out_prefix.with_suffix(".txt")
        # official line: "<image_path>, <crop score>..., <average score>"
        txt.write_text("".join(
            f"{r['filename']}, " + ", ".join(str(s) for s in r["crop_scores"])
            + f", {r['score']}\n"
            for r in rows
        ))
        return jsonl, txt

{"content": """"DPG-Bench tests -- no GPU/network; the VQA judge and image loading are faked."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

import pytest

from aqa.eval.dpgbench import (
    DpgBenchScorer,
    convert_dpg_csv,
    load_records,
    score_image,
    summarize,
)
from aqa.eval.harness.diffusion import DiffusionHarness
from aqa.eval.registry import BenchmarkRecipe, BenchmarkRegistry
from aqa.logging_util import AqaError


class _FakeImage:
    """Duck-typed PIL stand-in: crop returns a tagged copy (nothing else needed)."""

    def __init__(self, tag="full"):
        self.tag = tag

    def crop(self, box):
        return _FakeImage(tag=f"crop{box}")


class _FakeJudge:
    """Scripted VQA answers keyed by question text (default 'yes')."""

    def __init__(self, answers=None):
        self.answers = answers or {}
        self.calls = []

    def vqa(self, image, question):
        self.calls.append((image.tag, question))
        return self.answers.get(question, "yes")


def _record(idx, questions, prompt="p"):
    return {"idx": idx, "item_id": f"item{idx}", "prompt": prompt,
            "questions": questions, "category": questions[0]["category"]}


def _q(qid, question, dep, category="entity - whole"):
    return {"qid": qid, "question": question, "answer": f"{category} (x)",
            "dependency": dep, "category": category}


# ── converter ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def test_convert_dpg_csv(tmp_path):
    csv_path = tmp_path / "dpg_bench.csv"
    csv_path.write_text(
        "item_id,text,keywords,proposition_id,dependency,category_broad,"
        "category_detailed,tuple,question_natural_language\n"
        'a,"prompt A",,1,0,entity,whole,entity - whole (space),Is there space?\n'
        'a,"prompt A",,2,1,entity,whole,entity - whole (man),Is there a man?\n'
        'b,"prompt B",,1,0,attribute,color,attribute - color (red),Is it red?\n'
    )
    records = convert_dpg_csv(csv_path, tmp_path / "prompts.jsonl")
    # the first data row is skipped (upstream parity), so item 'a' has qid 2 only
    assert [r["item_id"] for r in records] == ["a", "b"]
    qa = records[0]["questions"]
    assert [q["qid"] for q in qa] == [2]
    assert qa[0]["dependency"] == [1]  # dangling parent, as upstream produces
    assert qa[0]["category"] == "entity - whole"
    assert records[0]["prompt"] == "prompt A"
    assert records[1]["questions"][0]["category"] == "attribute - color"
    # round-trip
    assert load_records(tmp_path / "prompts.jsonl") == records


def test_convert_dpg_csv_multi_dependency(tmp_path):
    csv_path = tmp_path / "dpg_bench.csv"
    csv_path.write_text(
        "item_id,text,keywords,proposition_id,dependency,category_broad,"
        "category_detailed,tuple,question_natural_language\n"
        'a,"prompt A",,1,0,entity,whole,entity - whole (x),Q1?\n'
        'a,"prompt A",,2,"1, 3",entity,whole,entity - whole (y),Q2?\n'
    )
    records = convert_dpg_csv(csv_path, tmp_path / "p.jsonl")
    assert records[0]["questions"][1]["dependency"] == [1, 3]


# ── per-image scoring (fake judge) ───────────────────────────────────────────
def test_score_image_all_yes():
    rec = _record(0, [_q(1, "q1?", [0]), _q(2, "q2?", [1])])
    result = score_image(_FakeJudge(), _FakeImage(), rec, resolution=1024)
    assert result["score"] == 1.0
    assert result["adj_scores"] == {1: 1.0, 2: 1.0}
    assert result["answers"] == {1: "yes", 2: "yes"}
    assert len(result["crop_scores"]) == 1  # pic_num=1: single top-left crop


def test_score_image_dependency_zeroing():
    # parent (q1) answers 'no' -> child (q2) zeroed in adjusted scores, raw kept
    rec = _record(0, [_q(1, "parent?", [0]), _q(2, "child?", [1])])
    result = score_image(_FakeJudge({"parent?": "no"}), _FakeImage(), rec,
                         resolution=1024)
    assert result["raw_scores"] == {1: 0.0, 2: 1.0}
    assert result["adj_scores"] == {1: 0.0, 2: 0.0}
    assert result["score"] == 0.0


def test_score_image_mixed_answers():
    rec = _record(0, [_q(1, "a?", [0]), _q(2, "b?", [0]), _q(3, "c?", [0])])
    result = score_image(_FakeJudge({"a?": "no"}), _FakeImage(), rec,
                         resolution=1024)
    assert result["score"] == pytest.approx(2 / 3)


def test_score_image_dangling_dependency_raises():
    rec = _record(0, [_q(2, "child?", [1])])  # parent qid 1 absent
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        score_image(_FakeJudge(), _FakeImage(), rec, resolution=1024)


def test_score_image_pic_num_quadrants():
    judge = _FakeJudge()
    rec = _record(0, [_q(1, "q?", [0])])
    result = score_image(judge, _FakeImage(), rec, resolution=512, pic_num=4)
    assert len(result["crop_scores"]) == 4
    # all four official quadrant crops were judged
    tags = {tag for tag, _ in judge.calls}
    assert "crop((0, 0, 512, 512))" in tags
    assert "crop((512, 512, 1024, 1024))" in tags


# ── evaluate_rows + summarize ────────────────────────────────────────────────
def _image_row(idx):
    return {"idx": str(idx), "prompt": "p", "image_path": f"/x/{idx:04d}.png",
            "seed": "42"}


def test_evaluate_rows_skips_failures_and_gaps():
    recs = [
        _record(0, [_q(1, "ok?", [0])]),
        _record(1, [_q(2, "dangling?", [1])]),  # KeyError -> skipped (upstream parity)
    ]
    judge = _FakeJudge()
    scorer = DpgBenchScorer(judge=judge)
    rows = scorer.evaluate_rows(
        [_image_row(0), _image_row(1), _image_row(2)],  # idx 2 has no record
        recs, image_loader=lambda path: _FakeImage(),
    )
    assert [r["idx"] for r in rows] == [0]
    assert rows[0]["score"] == 1.0
    assert rows[0]["item_id"] == "item0"
    assert rows[0]["categories"] == {1: "entity - whole"}


def test_summarize_official_formula_quirk():
    """Categories aggregate RAW (pre-dependency) scores; overall uses adjusted."""
    rec = _record(0, [_q(1, "parent?", [0]), _q(2, "child?", [1])],
                  prompt="p")
    judge = _FakeJudge({"parent?": "no"})

## Deviations / ambiguities found in the official scoring (and how I resolved them)

1. **Row-0 skip is an upstream bug** (`if i == 0: continue` in `prepare_dpg_data` — pandas already handles the header). It drops qid 1 of `partiprompts97`, leaving dangling dependencies (qids 2,3,4,5,12–15 reference parent 1), so upstream's per-image `try/except` silently drops that whole image. Ported bug-for-bug (converter skips row 0; scorer's KeyError on the dangling parent → warn + skip image) because score parity with the published anchor (88.14) requires it.
2. **Category breakdown uses pre-dependency (raw) scores while the headline uses post-dependency** — upstream returns `qid2scores_orig` for categories. Kept both maps; `per_sample` uses the *adjusted* scores (they match the headline metric's granularity; raw would inflate pass rates for stats).
3. **`pic_num=1` judges only the top-left `resolution`² crop**, not the whole image — upstream default behavior; harmless when generation size == resolution (crop = full image), which is why the recipe pins `resolution: 1024` alongside the harness's default 1024² generation. `pic_num` stays a scorer parameter for fidelity but is not exposed in the recipe (we always generate 1 image/prompt).
4. **Official score output is a flat txt**; we write a byte-compatible `.txt` (`image_path, crop scores…, average`) *plus* a richer `.jsonl` (answers, both score maps, categories) — diffable against upstream, but self-describing.
5. **`evaluate_rows` gained an `image_loader` seam** (defaults to lazy `Image.open`) because the test venv has no PIL; production behavior identical, tests stay PIL-free.

## Goal

`executor.type: local` today runs the pipeline in-process in whatever Python environment launched `aqa` (`aqa/executors/local.py` — 50 lines, trivial). Make it declarative like the ssh path: the user only edits yaml. Three modes:

```yaml
executor:
  type: local
  env:
    type: current        # DEFAULT, exactly today's in-process behavior
    # type: venv         # run the pipeline inside a (possibly provisioned) venv
    # path: ~/.venv-aqa-gpu
    # packages: auto     # "auto" = derive from run config; or explicit list[str]
    # type: docker       # build/run a local container (reuse executor.image)
    required_env: [HF_TOKEN]   # fast-fail preflight for ALL modes (empty default)
```

## Design decisions (follow these)

1. **Config** (`aqa/config.py`): add `EnvConfig(BaseModel, extra="forbid")` with `type: Literal["current","venv","docker"]="current"`, `path: str|None`, `packages: str|list[str]="auto"`, `create: bool=True`, `mounts: list[str]=[]` (docker extra bind mounts). `ExecutorConfig` gains `env: EnvConfig = Field(default_factory=EnvConfig)` and `required_env: list[str] = []`. Validators: venv requires `path`; docker leaves image config in existing `executor.image`; `packages` accepts "auto" or a list.

2. **Dispatch architecture**: keep in-process ONLY for `env.type=current`. For venv/docker, stage an inner run mirroring the ssh path (`aqa/executors/_remote.py` is the reference, reuse its helpers — import, don't copy):
   - Build an inner run yaml: copy the RunConfig but force `executor={"type":"local","num_gpus":<derived>}` and drop the env block (NO recursion into env dispatch). 1	"""LocalExecutor: run the quantize -> evaluate -> report pipeline in-process.
2	
3	This is the reference executor that lets the framework run on any machine that
4	can already reach the GPU (or inside a container), with no reservation system or
5	multi-hop SSH -- the open-source baseline path.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import json
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	from ..logging_util import get_logger
14	from ..pipeline import run_pipeline
15	from . import ProcessState, RunResult
16	
17	_log = get_logger("executor.local")
18	_META = "aqa_run.json"
19	
20	
21	class LocalExecutor:
22	    name = "local"
23	
24	    def __init__(self, **options):
25	        self.options = options
26	
27	    def run(self, run_cfg, *, dry_run: bool = False, resume: bool = False) -> RunResult:
28	        out_dir = Path(run_cfg.output.dir)
29	        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
30	        meta_path = out_dir / _META
31	        meta_path.write_text(json.dumps({"model": run_cfg.model, "state": "running"}))
32	        if dry_run:
33	            _log.info("[dry-run] would run pipeline for %s in %s", run_cfg.model, out_dir)
34	            return RunResult(output_dir=out_dir, state=ProcessState.DONE)
35	        state = run_pipeline(run_cfg, out_dir)
36	        meta_path.write_text(json.dumps({"model": run_cfg.model, "state": state.value}))
37	        return RunResult(output_dir=out_dir, state=state)
38	
39	    def status(self, output_dir: Path) -> ProcessState:
40	        meta = Path(output_dir) / _META
41	        if not meta.exists():
42	            return ProcessState.UNKNOWN
43	        return ProcessState(json.loads(meta.read_text()).get("state", "unknown"))
44	
45	    def stop(self, output_dir: Path) -> bool:
46	        return False  # in-process; nothing to signal
47	
48	    @staticmethod
49	    def detect(output_dir: Path) -> bool:
50	        return (Path(output_dir) / _META).exists()

1	"""Run a subprocess while *teeing* its output: live to this process's stdout
2	(so it streams back over the SSH channel in real time) and to a persisted log
3	file (for debugging / upload).
4	
5	The previous behaviour redirected a long tool's (lm_eval / auto-round) output
6	entirely into a log file, so a remote ``aqa run`` looked hung for the many
7	minutes of model load + eval even though the GPU was busy.  Streaming fixes that.
8	
9	A pseudo-terminal is allocated for the child by default so terminal-aware tools
10	(tqdm progress bars, vllm) render live and stay line-buffered; a plain pipe is
11	used as a fallback where a pty is unavailable.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import os
17	import select
18	import signal
19	import subprocess
20	import sys
21	import time
22	from pathlib import Path
23	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
24	
25	if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover
26	    from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
27	
28	TIMEOUT_RC = 124  # conventional exit code for a wall-clock timeout (matches `timeout(1)`)
29	
30	
31	def _emit(data: bytes) -> None:
32	    """Best-effort write of raw bytes to this process's stdout."""
33	    try:
34	        os.write(sys.stdout.fileno(), data)
35	    except (OSError, ValueError):  # stdout not backed by a real fd (captured)
36	        try:
37	            sys.stdout.write(data.decode(errors="replace"))
38	            sys.stdout.flush()
39	        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001, S110 - never let tee-logging kill the run
40	            pass
41	
42	
43	def _kill_tree(proc: subprocess.Popen) -> None:
44	    """Terminate the child's whole process group (agents spawn sub-processes)."""
45	    try:
46	        os.killpg(os.getpgid(proc.pid), signal.SIGTERM)
47	    except (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError, OSError):
48	        try:
49	            proc.terminate()
50	        except OSError:
51	            return
52	    try:
53	        proc.wait(timeout=10)
54	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
55	        try:
56	            os.killpg(os.getpgid(proc.pid), signal.SIGKILL)
57	        except OSError:
58	            proc.kill()
59	
60	
61	def _stream_pipe(
62	    cmd: Sequence[str], log_file, env: Mapping[str, str] | None,
63	    timeout: float | None,
64	) -> int:
65	    proc = subprocess.Popen(
66	        list(cmd),
67	        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
68	        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
69	        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
70	        env=dict(env) if env is not None else None,
71	        bufsize=0,
72	        start_new_session=True,
73	    )
74	    assert proc.stdout is not None
75	    deadline = (time.monotonic() + timeout) if timeout else None
76	    fd = proc.stdout.fileno()
77	    while True:
78	        if deadline is not None and time.monotonic() > deadline:
79	            _emit_timeout(log_file, timeout)
80	            _kill_tree(proc)
81	            return TIMEOUT_RC
82	        rlist, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.2)
83	        if fd in rlist:
84	            chunk = os.read(fd, 65536)
85	            if not chunk:
86	                break
87	            log_file.write(chunk)
88	            log_file.flush()
89	            _emit(chunk)
90	        elif proc.poll() is not None:
91	            break
92	    return proc.wait()
93	
94	
95	def _stream_pty(
96	    cmd: Sequence[str], log_file, env: Mapping[str, str] | None,
97	    timeout: float | None,
98	) -> int:
99	    import pty
100	
101	    master, slave = pty.openpty()
102	    proc = subprocess.Popen(
103	        list(cmd),
104	        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
105	        stdout=slave,
106	        stderr=slave,
107	        env=dict(env) if env is not None else None,
108	        close_fds=True,
109	        start_new_session=True,
110	    )
111	    os.close(slave)
112	    deadline = (time.monotonic() + timeout) if timeout else None
113	    try:
114	        while True:
115	            if deadline is not None and time.monotonic() > deadline:
116	                _emit_timeout(log_file, timeout)
117	                _kill_tree(proc)
118	                return TIMEOUT_RC
119	            try:
120	                rlist, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
121	            except InterruptedError:  # pragma: no cover - signal during select
122	                continue
123	            if master in rlist:
124	                try:
125	                    data = os.read(master, 65536)
126	                except OSError:  # EIO on Linux once the child's slave closes
127	                    break
128	                if not data:
129	                    break
130	                log_file.write(data)
131	                log_file.flush()
132	                _emit(data)
133	            elif proc.poll() is not None:
134	                break
135	    finally:
136	        os.close(master)
137	    return proc.wait()
138	
139	
140	def _emit_timeout(log_file, timeout: float | None) -> None:
141	    msg = f"\n[TIMEOUT] process exceeded {timeout}s\n".encode()
142	    log_file.write(msg)
143	    log_file.flush()
144	    _emit(msg)
145	
146	
147	def stream_subprocess(
148	    cmd: Sequence[str],
149	    log_path: str | Path,
150	    *,
151	    env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
152	    use_pty: bool = True,
153	    timeout: float | None = None,
154	) -> int:
155	    """Run ``cmd``, teeing combined stdout/stderr to stdout and ``log_path``.
156	
157	    Returns the child's exit code (or :data:`TIMEOUT_RC` when ``timeout`` elapses,
158	    after killing the child's process group).  ``use_pty`` allocates a
159	    pseudo-terminal so progress bars render live; it falls back to a pipe
160	    automatically where a pty cannot be created (e.g. non-POSIX platforms).
161	    """
162	    path = Path(log_path)
163	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
164	    with path.open("wb") as log_file:
165	        if use_pty and hasattr(os, "openpty"):
166	            try:
167	                return _stream_pty(cmd, log_file, env, timeout)
168	            except OSError:  # pragma: no cover - pty exhaustion / unsupported
169	                pass
170	        return _stream_pipe(cmd, log_file, env, timeout)

132	    """Connect a paramiko client, falling back to keyboard-interactive for
133	    password auth against servers that only offer that method (PAM)."""

197	def _sftp_fetch_tree(
198	    sftp, remote_dir: str, local_dir: Path, *, max_bytes: int = 500 * 1024 * 1024
199	) -> int:
200	    """Recursively download ``remote_dir`` into ``local_dir``; return file count.
201	
202	    Skips weights/caches (the same set excluded from result uploads) so we never
203	    drag multi-GB ``.safetensors`` back over SFTP -- that both wastes bandwidth and
204	    can stall paramiko's prefetch indefinitely (the run's own hf_dataset sink is
205	    what publishes results; this fetch is only for local log/json inspection). A
206	    ``max_bytes`` backstop skips any unexpectedly large blob rather than hanging.
207	
208	    Silently returns 0 if the remote dir does not exist (e.g. run failed before
209	    producing any results).
210	    """
211	    import stat as _stat
212	
213	    from ..report.scrub import EXCLUDED_DIRS, EXCLUDED_SUFFIXES
214	
215	    try:
216	        entries = sftp.listdir_attr(remote_dir)
217	    except OSError:
218	        return 0
219	    count = 0
220	    local_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
221	    for entry in entries:
222	        rpath = f"{remote_dir}/{entry.filename}"
223	        lpath = local_dir / entry.filename
224	        if _stat.S_ISDIR(entry.st_mode):
225	            if entry.filename in EXCLUDED_DIRS:
226	                _log.info("skipping excluded dir %s", rpath)
227	                continue
228	            count += _sftp_fetch_tree(sftp, rpath, lpath, max_bytes=max_bytes)
229	        elif not _stat.S_ISREG(entry.st_mode):
230	            _log.info("skipping non-regular file %s", rpath)  # fifo/socket/device
231	        elif Path(entry.filename).suffix.lower() in EXCLUDED_SUFFIXES:
232	            _log.info("skipping weight/blob %s", rpath)
233	        elif entry.st_size is not None and entry.st_size > max_bytes:
234	            _log.warning("skipping oversized file %s (%d bytes)", rpath, entry.st_size)
235	        else:
236	            try:
237	                sftp.get(rpath, str(lpath))
238	                count += 1
239	            except OSError:
240	                _log.warning("could not fetch %s", rpath)
241	    return count

244	def _exec_stream(client, command: str, *, poll: float = 0.5) -> int:
245	    """Run ``command`` remotely, streaming combined stdout/stderr live; return rc.
246	
247	    lm_eval / vllm report progress with tqdm bars that use carriage returns
248	    (``\\r``) instead of newlines, and phases like model load or a long eval run
249	    for minutes emitting no ``\\n`` at all.  Splitting only on ``\\n`` therefore
250	    makes those phases look hung (while the GPU is clearly busy).  We instead:
251	
252	      * treat both ``\\r`` and ``\\n`` as line delimiters, so each progress update
253	        surfaces as it arrives, and
254	      * block on ``recv`` with a short timeout (no busy-poll) and, when the stream
255	        goes briefly idle, flush any pending partial line so a paused progress bar
256	        or newline-less prompt still shows up.
257	    """
258	    chan = client.get_transport().open_session()
259	    chan.get_pty()
260	    chan.exec_command(command)
261	    chan.settimeout(poll)
262	    buf = b""
263	    while True:
264	        try:
265	            data = chan.recv(65536)
266	        except TimeoutError:
267	            data = b""
268	        if data:
269	            buf += data
270	            parts = re.split(rb"[\r\n]", buf)
271	            buf = parts.pop()  # trailing partial line; completes on a later read
272	            for line in parts:
273	                if line:
274	                    _log.info("[remote] %s", line.decode(errors="replace"))
275	        else:
276	            if buf:
277	                _log.info("[remote] %s", buf.decode(errors="replace"))
278	                buf = b""
279	            if chan.exit_status_ready():
280	                break
281	    if buf:
282	        _log.info("[remote] %s", buf.decode(errors="replace"))
283	    return chan.recv_exit_status()

89	def ensure_device_map(cmd: str, cfg: QuantConfig, num_gpus: int) -> str:
90	    """Append ``--device_map <value>`` to an agent-built command when missing.
91	
92	    Keeps the agent-optimize path multi-GPU aware without overriding a device_map
93	    the agent (or the user via ``quant.device_map``) already chose.
94	    """
95	    device_map = resolve_device_map(cfg, num_gpus)
96	    if not device_map or "--device_map" in shlex.split(cmd):
97	        return cmd
98	    return f"{cmd} --device_map {shlex.quote(device_map)}"

101	def _run_autoround(cmd: list[str], output_dir: Path) -> Path:
102	    _log.info("[CMD] %s", " ".join(shlex.quote(c) for c in cmd))
103	    if shutil.which("auto-round") is None:
104	        raise AqaError("auto-round is not installed; `pip install auto-round`")
105	    log_path = output_dir / "quantize.log"
106	    from ..proc import stream_subprocess
107	
108	    rc = stream_subprocess(cmd, log_path)
109	    if rc != 0:
110	        raise AqaError(f"quantization failed (rc={rc}); see {log_path}")
111	    return output_dir
112

114	# ── diffusion post-export repair ──────────────────────────────────────────────
115	# auto-round saves the non-quantized pipeline components (text_encoder, vae, ...)
116	# itself, and can mangle them: Z-Image's Qwen3 text encoder is re-saved with the
117	# inner `model.` prefix stripped from every weight, which breaks vllm-omni's
118	# loader ("no module or parameter named 'text_encoder.embed_tokens'").  These
119	# components are never quantized, so the safe repair is to restore the pristine
120	# directory from the source model whenever the exported one does not match.
121	
122	_QUANTIZED_COMPONENTS = ("transformer", "unet")
123	
124	
125	def _safetensors_keys(path: Path) -> set[str] | None:
126	    """Union of tensor keys across all shards (header-only read). None if n/a."""
127	    try:
128	        from safetensors import safe_open
129	    except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - quant stack always has safetensors
130	        _log.warning("safetensors unavailable; skipping export component verification")
131	        return None
132	    keys: set[str] = set()
133	    shards = sorted(path.glob("*.safetensors"))
134	    if not shards:
135	        return set() if (path / "config.json").exists() else None
136	    for shard in shards:
137	        try:
138	            with safe_open(str(shard), framework="numpy") as fh:
139	                keys.update(fh.keys())
140	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - corrupt/partial shard
141	            _log.warning("could not read %s: %s", shard, exc)
142	            return None
143	    return keys

59	## Quick start
60	
61	```bash
62	aqa list                          # benchmarks + registered plugins
63	aqa validate examples/run.yaml    # type-check a run config, no execution
64	aqa run examples/run.yaml         # quantize -> evaluate -> gate (local executor)
65	aqa run examples/run.yaml --dry-run
66	aqa eval examples/eval_only.yaml --out ./results     # evaluate only
67	aqa compare ./results/base ./results/cand            # score deltas
68	```
69	
70	## One file describes a run (`run.yaml`)
71	
72	```yaml
73	model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
74	provider: { type: quantize, quant: { scheme: MXFP4, method: model_free } }
75	eval: { benchmarks: [piqa, hellaswag, gsm8k], backend: vllm, baseline: true }
76	gate: { max_accuracy_drop: 0.02 }          # NO-GO if quantized drops > 2%
77	agent: { fix_loop: true, optimize: true, tiers: [openclaw, minimax, opus] }
78	executor: { type: local }                  # local | ssh | intel_reserve (plugin)
79	output: { dir: ./results/run, sinks: [ { type: local_fs } ] }
80	```
81	
82	Composition: `_base_: other.yaml` (inherit + deep-merge, `null` deletes),
83	`${VAR}` / `${VAR:-default}` env expansion. **Secrets are only referenced via
84	`*_env` variables, never inlined** (open-source hard constraint).
85	
86	## Model providers: evaluation is the core, quantization is a plugin
87	
88	The framework is **eval-centric**: the primary job is to *evaluate a model*; how
89	that model is produced/served is a pluggable **`provider`** that cleanly separates
90	the *served target* from the *benchmark*.
91	
92	| `provider.type` | What it evaluates |
93	|---|---|
94	| `pretrained` (default) | a HF repo id / local path, as-is |
95	| `quantize` | runs autoquant (optionally agent-optimize + fix-loop), then evaluates the quantized checkpoint |
96	| `endpoint` | an already-served OpenAI-compatible endpoint (agentic path) |
97	
98	```yaml
99	# eval-only (default provider is `pretrained`):
100	model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
101	eval: { benchmarks: [piqa, gsm8k], backend: vllm }
102	
103	# quantize-then-eval (quantization is now just a provider):
104	provider: { type: quantize, quant: { scheme: MXFP4, method: model_free } }
105	
106	# evaluate a served endpoint:
107	provider: { type: endpoint, base_url: http://host:8000/v1, served_model: org/m,
108	            api_key_env: MY_API_KEY }
109	```
110	
111	**Backward compatible.** Older quant-centric configs that put `quant:` at the top
112	level keep working unchanged — the loader folds a top-level `quant:` into
113	`provider: {type: quantize, quant: {...}}`, and `run_cfg.quant` still returns the
114	quantize provider's config. `examples/run_5000.yaml` runs as before. Add your own
115	provider via the `aqa.providers` entry-point group.
116	
117	### Customizing the quantization algorithm
118	
119	The `quant:` block maps onto the [`auto-round`](https://github.com/intel/auto-round)
120	CLI. Beyond `method` / `scheme` / `iters`, you can pick and **compose** the
121	underlying algorithm(s) via `algorithm:` (a comma-separated chain, mapped to
122	`--algorithm`):
123	
124	| `quant:` field | auto-round flag | Purpose |
125	|---|---|---|
126	| `method: model_free` | `--model_free` | calibration-free, weight-only (RTN) fast path |
127	| `algorithm: rtn` | `--algorithm rtn` | round-to-nearest block quantizer |
128	| `algorithm: auto_round` | `--algorithm auto_round` | SignRound iterative tuning (use with `iters: 200`) |
129	| `algorithm: awq` | `--algorithm awq` | AWQ activation-aware smoothing (preprocessor) |
130	| `algorithm: hadamard` | `--algorithm hadamard` | Hadamard rotation (preprocessor) |
131	| `algorithm: svdquant` | `--algorithm svdquant` | SVD low-rank decomposition (preprocessor) |
132	| `enable_alg_ext: true` | `--enable_alg_ext` | experimental SignRound extension ("auto-round v2") |
133	| `hadamard_type: quarot_hadamard` | `--rotation-hadamard-type` | Hadamard variant: `hadamard` / `random_hadamard` / `quarot_hadamard` |
134	| `opt_rtn: true` / `false` | `--enable_opt_rtn` / `--disable_opt_rtn` | RTN optimized rounding toggle |
135	
136	**Composition rules** (enforced at config-load time, mirroring auto-round):
137	`awq`, `hadamard`, `svdquant` are **preprocessors** — they may be *stacked* and are
138	applied left-to-right *before* quantization. `rtn` and `auto_round` are **block
139	quantizers** — exactly one runs (omit and a default is supplied: `auto_round`, or
140	`rtn` when `iters: 0`). So:
141	
142	```yaml
143	# auto-round v2 tuning
144	provider: { type: quantize, quant: { scheme: W4A16, algorithm: auto_round,
145	                                     iters: 200, enable_alg_ext: true } }
146	
147	# AWQ smoothing then SignRound tuning
148	quant: { scheme: W4A16, algorithm: "awq,auto_round", iters: 200 }
149	
150	# stack two preprocessors (AWQ + Hadamard rotation) before the default quantizer
151	quant: { scheme: MXFP4, algorithm: "awq,hadamard", hadamard_type: quarot_hadamard }
152	
153	# pure optimized RTN
154	quant: { scheme: W4A16, algorithm: rtn, opt_rtn: true }
155	```
156	
157	Valid: `rtn`, `auto_round`, `awq`, `hadamard`, `svdquant`, `awq,auto_round`,
158	`hadamard,auto_round`, `svdquant,rtn`, `awq,hadamard`, `awq,hadamard,auto_round`.
159	Invalid: `rtn,auto_round` (two block quantizers → rejected).
160	
161	
162	### Remote dispatch: NVIDIA CUDA or Intel XPU
163	
164	The `ssh` executor runs the whole pipeline inside a container on a remote host.
165	`executor.ssh.accelerator` (`cuda` default, or `xpu`) switches the device flags
166	and default base image — no other config changes:
167	
168	```yaml
169	executor:
170	  type: ssh
171	  image: { xpu: vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:nightly }   # or `gpu:` for CUDA
172	  ssh:
173	    host: sdp@192.168.11.2
174	    gpus: "0,1"                 # cuda -> --gpus device=; xpu -> ZE_AFFINITY_MASK
175	    accelerator: xpu            # cuda | xpu
176	    auth: { method: password, password_env: B60_SSH_PASS }
177	    jump: [ ... ]               # optional multi-hop chain
178	```
179	
180	- **cuda** → NGC base + `--gpus '"device=<ids>"'`, installs matching `vllm`.
181	- **xpu** → `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu` base + `/dev/dri` passthrough, `--privileged`,
182	  `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=<ids>`, `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`. The base image
183	  already ships `vllm-xpu`, so aqa does **not** reinstall CUDA `vllm` (only
184	  `auto-round` + `lm-eval` on top). See `examples/run_b60_xpu.yaml`.
185	
186	`image.dockerfile: local` builds the accelerator-appropriate shipped Dockerfile —
187	`docker/gpu.dockerfile` (NGC) for CUDA, `docker/xpu.dockerfile` (Intel base) for
188	XPU — each adding tooling + Node + OpenClaw for the fix-loop. Omit `dockerfile` to
189	run the base image directly (Node/OpenClaw are then installed at runtime).
190	
191	## Evaluation: harnesses, task grouping, and model_args
192	
193	`eval` selects a **harness** (`lm_eval` default, `native`, or `evalscope` plugin)
194	and an infra **backend** (`hf` | `vllm`). Harness-specific knobs live in per-method
195	blocks so the eval methods stay cleanly separated:
196	
197	```yaml
198	eval:
199	  benchmarks: [piqa, hellaswag, mmlu, gsm8k]
200	  backend: vllm
201	  harness: lm_eval
202	  lm_eval:
203	    model_args: { enable_thinking: false, reasoning_parser: qwen3, max_num_seqs: 128 }
204	    gen_kwargs: { max_gen_toks: 2048 }   # default --gen_kwargs for generative tasks

343	## Architecture
344	
345	```
346	aqa/
347	  config.py        typed RunConfig + run.yaml composer (single parse point)
348	  registry.py      entry-point plugin registries (7 extension points)
349	  pipeline.py      provide-model -> evaluate (+ baseline) -> gate -> sinks
350	  cli.py           run / eval / swebench / validate / list / compare
351	  providers/       pretrained | quantize | endpoint  (model-under-eval source)
352	  eval/
353	    scoring.py     native scorer library (see NOTICE for attributions)
354	    dataset.py     hf://…?split= URI loading + prompt templating
355	    registry.py    benchmark recipe schema + loader
356	    runner.py      orchestrate benchmarks across harnesses/backends
357	    harness/       native | lm_eval  (evalscope via optional plugin)
358	  backends/        hf | vllm  (vllm_xpu via plugin)
359	  executors/       local | ssh  (intel_reserve via plugin)
360	  report/          sinks (local_fs | hf_dataset) + gate/compare
361	  quantize/        auto-round command builder + runner
362	  agent/           fix-loop / patch / knowledge (replay) / optimize (Python orchestration)
363	  agent_eval/      E0-E3: client / endpoint / solver / ReAct / environment
364	  sandbox/         local | docker  (tool-use / terminal execution)
365	  terminal_bench/  E4 self-contained terminal tasks (YAML + verifier)
366	  swebench/        SWE-bench Verified adapter (dataset/spec/env/report/run)
367	recipes/           benchmarks/*.yaml, schemes/*.yaml, quant/*.json (pinned)
368	skills/            quantize / evaluate / fix-and-patch  (SKILL.md for agents)
369	docs/              design docs + source-verified auto-round references
370	```
371	
372	### Extension points (add a plugin = pip package, no fork)
373	
374	| entry-point group | add a new… |
375	|---|---|
376	| `aqa.providers`     | model-under-eval source (e.g. `distill`, `lora_merge`) |
377	| `aqa.harnesses`     | evaluation framework (e.g. `evalscope`) |
378	| `aqa.backends`      | inference infra (e.g. `vllm_xpu`) |
379	| `aqa.executors`     | machine access (e.g. `intel_reserve`) |

381	| `aqa.recipe_stores` | recipe source/sink |
382	| `aqa.scorers`       | scoring function |

384	New benchmark = drop a `recipes/benchmarks/<name>.yaml` (+ a `.py` scorer only

387	## Skills

440	def _load_raw(path: Path, _seen: set[Path]) -> dict:
441	    """Load a YAML file, resolving a single ``_base_`` chain (relative to the file)."""
442	    path = path.resolve()
443	    if path in _seen:
444	        raise ConfigError(f"circular _base_ reference at {path}")
445	    _seen.add(path)
446	    if not path.exists():
447	        raise ConfigError(f"config file not found: {path}")
448	    data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text()) or {}
449	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
450	        raise ConfigError(f"config root must be a mapping: {path}")
451	    base_ref = data.pop("_base_", None)
452	    if base_ref:
453	        base_path = (path.parent / base_ref).resolve()
454	        base_data = _load_raw(base_path, _seen)
455	        data = _deep_merge(base_data, data)
456	    return data

459	def _resolve_context(agent: dict, base_dir: Path) -> None:
460	    """Resolve an ``agent.context: "@file"`` reference into inline text."""
461	    ctx = agent.get("context")
462	    if isinstance(ctx, str) and ctx.startswith("@"):
463	        ctx_path = (base_dir / ctx[1:]).resolve()
464	        if not ctx_path.exists():
465	            raise ConfigError(f"agent.context file not found: {ctx_path}")
466	        agent["context"] = ctx_path.read_text()

469	def _normalize_provider(raw: dict) -> dict:
470	    """Fold a legacy top-level ``quant:`` block into ``provider: {type: quantize}``.
471	
472	    Eval-centric configs use ``provider:``; older quant-centric run.yaml files put
473	    ``quant:`` at the top level.  This shim keeps those working unchanged: a
474	    top-level ``quant`` becomes the quantize provider's config.  Raises if a config
475	    sets both ``quant:`` and a non-quantize ``provider:`` (ambiguous intent).
476	    """
477	    if not isinstance(raw, dict) or "quant" not in raw:
478	        return raw
479	    quant = raw.pop("quant")
480	    if quant is None:  # explicit `quant: null` => eval-only, just drop it.
481	        return raw
482	    provider = raw.get("provider")
483	    if provider is None:
484	        raw["provider"] = {"type": "quantize", "quant": quant}
485	    elif isinstance(provider, dict):
486	        ptype = provider.get("type", "quantize")
487	        if ptype != "quantize":
488	            raise ConfigError(
489	                f"config sets top-level `quant:` but provider.type={ptype!r}; "
490	                "move quant under `provider: {type: quantize, quant: {...}}`"
491	            )
492	        provider.setdefault("type", "quantize")
493	        provider.setdefault("quant", quant)
494	    return raw

497	def load_run_config(path: str | Path) -> RunConfig:
498	    """Load, compose, env-expand, and validate a ``run.yaml`` into a RunConfig."""
499	    p = Path(path)
500	    raw = _load_raw(p, set())
501	    raw = _expand_env(raw)
502	    raw = _normalize_provider(raw)
503	    if isinstance(raw.get("agent"), dict):
504	        _resolve_context(raw["agent"], p.resolve().parent)
505	    try:
506	        return RunConfig.model_validate(raw)
507	    except Exception as exc:  # pydantic ValidationError -> ConfigError
508	        raise ConfigError(f"invalid run config {p}: {exc}") from exc

1	# Self-contained GPU image for `aqa` remote dispatch (executor.type=ssh, image.dockerfile=local).
2	#
3	# Built + run by aqa/executors/ssh.py when `executor.image.dockerfile: local`.
4	# It sits on top of an NVIDIA NGC PyTorch base image so the CUDA toolkit (nvcc 13.x)
5	# is on PATH and flashinfer / vLLM JIT kernels compile for modern GPUs (sm_90a/H200)
6	# instead of hitting the CUDA-12.0 `FlagHeads` failure of an apt `nvidia-cuda-toolkit`.
7	#
8	# The image installs only OS tooling + `uv`; the actual quant/eval stack
9	# (auto-round, lm-eval, vllm, aqa itself) is installed at container runtime from the
10	# staged repo, so the image stays stable while the framework iterates.
11	#
12	# Override the base at build time:
13	#   docker build --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.10-py3 ...
14	# or in run.yaml:  executor.image.gpu: nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.10-py3
15	#
16	# NGC images are large (~20 GB) and need a recent NVIDIA driver on the host; verify
17	# `docker run --gpus all <base> nvidia-smi` on the target box first.
18	ARG BASE_IMAGE=nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.01-py3
19	FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}
20	
21	ENV LANG=C.UTF-8 \
22	    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
23	    HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 \
24	    TQDM_MININTERVAL=120
25	
26	# uv (fast Python package manager) used by the container bootstrap to install the stack.
27	COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
28	
29	# CLI tools the pipeline expects (NGC ships build-essential/git/curl already).
30	RUN apt-get update && \
31	    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
32	        git jq unzip curl zip ca-certificates wget numactl time xz-utils && \
33	    apt-get clean && \
34	    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
35	
36	# Node.js v22 + the OpenClaw agent-fix backend (parity with local_dispatch's
37	# agent image). OpenClaw is the default tier-0 fix backend; the Copilot CLI is
38	# added at container runtime only when a copilot-backed tier (opus/sonnet/minimax)
39	# is configured. Runtime provisioning (`python -m aqa.agent.provision`) lays the
40	# ~/.openclaw + ~/.copilot config down and syncs MINIMAX_API_KEY.
41	RUN curl -fsSL https://nodejs.org/dist/v22.20.0/node-v22.20.0-linux-x64.tar.xz \
42	        | tar -xJ --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local
43	RUN npm install -g openclaw@2026.6.8 && npm cache clean --force
44	
45	WORKDIR /workspace
46	
47	# No ENTRYPOINT: ssh.py runs the container with `--entrypoint bash` + a staged
48	# bootstrap that pip-installs the repo and runs `aqa run` with executor.type=local.

Full RFC: https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/main/rfcs/0001-trajectory-format.md — fetch it if you need more detail.

- **fix-loop trajectories**: `aqa/agent/trajectories.py` (`TrajectoryStore`, per-phase JSONL under the knowledge root, distilled successful-fix summaries: signature/error_class/root_cause/fix_rationale/component/smoke_test/tried_and_rejected/tier/steps/model_id/scheme/method/run_id) and `aqa/agent/knowledge.py` (`KnowledgeStore` — patches archived by signature hash; read it to find how to retrieve a patch's diff text by signature).
